name: View local SMB users
description: Display local Windows (SMB) user configurations for all SVMs, a specific SVM or a specific user.

name: View members of a local SMB group
description: List the users and groups that are members of a specific local Windows (SMB) group.

name: View name mappings
description: Retrieve name-mapping configurations for all SVMs or for a specific SVM, direction and index.

name: View NetBIOS aliases of an SMB server
description: Displays the list of NetBIOS aliases configured on an SMB server.

name: View NetBIOS over TCP information for SMB servers
description: Display NetBIOS over TCP information for SMB servers on one SVM or all SVMs: registered NetBIOS names, interfaces, and WINS server state.

name: View NFSv4 storepool blocked clients
description: Clients blocked for exceeding NFSv4 storepool limits are listed.

name: View open SMB files
description: Displays information about files open over SMB sessions, including continuous availability status.

name: View preferred domain controllers
description: Retrieve the preferred domain controller configuration of an SVM.

name: View restricted group GPOs
description: Displays the restricted group Group Policy Objects defined in Active Directory or applied to the SMB server.

name: View security trace results
description: The results captured by security trace filters are displayed.

name: View SMB domain information
description: Show an SMB server's domain information, including the domain controllers and other servers it has discovered, for one SVM or all SVMs.

name: View SMB home directory search paths
description: Display the SMB (CIFS) home directory search path configuration for one SVM or for all SVMs in the cluster.

name: View SMB server configuration
description: The SMB server configuration of one SVM or all SVMs is displayed.

name: View SMB sessions
description: Display information about established SMB sessions on an SVM, such as client IP, IP family, user type, and whether the session is encrypted or signed.

name: View SMB share ACLs
description: The share-level ACL entries of an SMB share, or the entry for a specific user or group, are displayed.

name: View SMB shares
description: List SMB shares on SVMs or display a specific share's configuration.

name: View SMB user home directory paths
description: Displays the home directory path resolved for a given SMB user.

name: View the export policy netgroup queue and cache
description: The netgroup queue and netgroup cache used for export policy evaluation are displayed for troubleshooting.

name: View the junction path of a qtree
description: Shows the junction path through which a qtree is accessed.

name: View the netgroup file status of an SVM
description: Display the status of the netgroup file loaded on an SVM, including the per-node hash values, to confirm the netgroup definitions are consistent on every node.

name: View the preferred trusted domain list for name-mapping searches
description: Displays the preferred trusted domains used for multidomain name-mapping searches on an SMB server.

name: View trusted SMB domains
description: Displays the trusted domains discovered for an SMB server, optionally rediscovering trusts and retrieving the SMB domain configuration.

name: View UNIX group cache settings
description: The name-service cache settings for UNIX groups are displayed for all SVMs or one SVM.

name: View UNIX symlink mappings for SMB shares
description: The UNIX symbolic link mappings for SMB shares on one or all SVMs are retrieved.

name: View UNIX user cache settings
description: The name-service cache settings for UNIX users are displayed for all SVMs or one SVM.

name: View UNIX users and groups
description: List the host-specific UNIX users and groups configured on an SVM.

name: View volume mount and junction path information
description: Display where volumes are mounted in the NAS namespace, including junction paths.

name: View Windows users and groups
description: List the host-specific Windows users and groups configured on an SVM.

name: Write data to a file
description: Writes data to a new or existing file in a volume.

name: Add an I/O module or PCIe card
description: Install an additional I/O module or PCIe card, such as a RoCE-capable module for NVMe shelves, in a controller, then cable and configure its ports.

name: Add drives to a node or shelf
description: Physically install new drives into empty slots of a node or shelf, after checking compatibility in Hardware Universe, to increase storage capacity.

name: Boot the recovery image on the replacement boot media
description: From the LOADER prompt, boot the ONTAP recovery image from the partner or a USB flash drive to restore the image, var file system and environment variables to the new boot media, then give back the controller.

name: Cable the ISLs between MetroCluster FC sites
description: The FC switches at each site are connected through the inter-switch links using the cabling for the configuration.

name: Cable the management and data connections
description: The controller management and data ports are cabled to the management and data networks at each site.

name: Change a drive shelf ID
description: Set a drive shelf's ID to a new value using the shelf ID button.

name: Configure an Ethernet port for storage use
description: Set a RoCE-capable Ethernet port to storage mode so it can connect to storage shelves.

name: Give back the controller
description: The replacement controller is booted into ONTAP and gets its storage back from the partner, with automatic giveback re-enabled and encryption keys restored where needed, so the HA pair returns to normal operation.

name: Hot-add a drive shelf
description: Nondisruptively add a drive shelf (or stack of shelves) to a running HA pair, cluster or MetroCluster configuration by cabling the new shelf, setting its ID and assigning its drives.

name: Hot-add a stack of SAS disk shelves and FC-to-SAS bridges in a MetroCluster FC configuration
description: Nondisruptively add a new stack of SAS disk shelves together with a new pair of FC-to-SAS bridges to a MetroCluster FC configuration.

name: Hot-remove a drive shelf
description: Nondisruptively remove drive shelves whose drives no longer hold aggregates from a running system.

name: Install FC-to-SAS bridges and SAS disk shelves
description: FC-to-SAS bridges and SAS disk shelves are installed, verified for disk connectivity, and cabled to the controller FC ports or FC switches.

name: Power off a single MetroCluster site
description: Switch over to the remaining site and halt and power down the equipment at the site to be maintained or relocated.

name: Power off an entire MetroCluster configuration
description: Disable AUSO and halt and power down all nodes and components at both MetroCluster sites.

name: Power on a MetroCluster site and return to normal operation
description: Power on the switches, shelves, bridges and controllers of a powered-off site, reenable ISLs and return the configuration to normal operation.

name: Recable the system and reassign disks after controller replacement
description: Recable storage to the replacement controller, reassign disk ownership to its system ID, and give back storage so the system resumes normal operation.

name: Relocate a powered-off MetroCluster site
description: Physically relocate the equipment of a powered-off site, recable it and verify intersite ISL connectivity.

name: Remove a failed disk
description: Identifies a failed disk, locates it in the shelf and physically removes it.

name: Replace a caching module
description: Replace a failed Flash Cache caching module, by hot-swap or with the controller shut down, and bring the replacement online.

name: Replace a controller module
description: An impaired controller module is replaced by moving its components (PSUs, fans, DIMMs, NV battery, boot media, cards) into the new module and installing it. Licenses are then installed, LIFs verified, the serial number registered, MetroCluster aggregates switched back and the failed part returned.

name: Replace a DIMM
description: Shut down the impaired controller, remove the controller module, replace the failed system DIMM and reinstall the controller.

name: Replace a DIMM in a shelf NSM
description: Replace a failed DIMM inside an NVMe shelf module.

name: Replace a disk shelf drive drawer
description: Prepare the shelf, remove the cable chains and the failed drive drawer, and install a replacement drive drawer.

name: Replace a disk shelf nondisruptively in a MetroCluster configuration
description: Replace an entire disk shelf in a MetroCluster configuration without disrupting data access, moving its disks to the new shelf.

name: Replace a drive
description: Hot-swap a failed drive in a controller chassis or drive shelf and assign ownership of the replacement drive if needed.

name: Replace a drive shelf module
description: Hot-swap or replace an impaired shelf module (NSM or IOM) in a drive shelf.

name: Replace a failed software RAID drive
description: Identify and detach a failed drive in an ONTAP Select software RAID node and add a new drive as a spare.

name: Replace a fan module
description: Replace a failed fan module in a controller chassis or drive shelf.

name: Replace a field-replaceable unit in a switch
description: Replace a faulty field-replaceable unit in a switch by following the switch vendor's component replacement procedure.

name: Replace a FIPS drive or SED
description: Remove a failed FIPS drive or self-encrypting drive, install a new one and assign its ownership.

name: Replace a Flash Cache module carrier
description: Shut down the impaired node, replace the Flash Cache module carrier, reboot the controller and return the failed part.

name: Replace a MetroCluster FC switch
description: An impaired FC switch is fenced off, then replaced nondisruptively with a preconfigured switch, and the MetroCluster is verified.

name: Replace a pair of FC-to-SAS bridges to consolidate storage stacks
description: Replace a pair of older FC-to-SAS bridges with higher-capacity bridges and consolidate storage stacks behind the new pair, including cabling, zoning, and disabling unused ports.

name: Replace a power supply unit
description: Hot-swap a failed power supply unit in a controller chassis or drive shelf.

name: Replace a switch
description: Replace a failed Ethernet switch (cluster, storage, shared or MetroCluster IP) with a new switch and restore its configuration and connections without disrupting the cluster.

name: Replace a System Management module
description: Shut down the impaired controller, replace its System Management module, reboot it, give back storage and reinstall licenses and register the serial number.

name: Replace an FC-to-SAS bridge
description: Hot-swap a single FC-to-SAS (FibreBridge) bridge in a MetroCluster FC configuration with a replacement bridge of the same or a newer model.

name: Replace an I/O module or PCIe card
description: Replace a failed I/O module, PCIe card or mezzanine card, by hot-swap or with the controller shut down, and bring the replacement online.

name: Replace an LED USB module
description: Remove a failed LED USB module and install a replacement.

name: Replace CNA/UTA2 adapter optical modules
description: Replace the SFP+ optical modules on a CNA/UTA2 adapter with modules that match the adapter's chosen FC or CNA (Ethernet) personality.

name: Replace MetroCluster FC switches with a new vendor or model
description: Nondisruptively replace the FC switches in a MetroCluster FC configuration with switches of a new model or vendor.

name: Replace the boot media
description: Physically remove the failed boot media from the controller or system management module, install the replacement, and put the ONTAP boot image onto it.

name: Replace the boot media in a shelf NSM
description: Replace the failed boot media inside an NVMe shelf module.

name: Replace the chassis
description: A failed system chassis is swapped for a new one. The work covers preparation (locating the system, checking parts, labeling cables), moving the PSUs, fans, controllers, I/O modules and drives across, then setting the chassis HA state, switching back MetroCluster aggregates and returning the failed part.

name: Replace the Ethernet I/O module in a shelf NSM
description: Replace a failed Ethernet I/O module in an NVMe shelf module.

name: Replace the NV battery
description: Replace the failed battery that backs the controller's non-volatile memory (NVRAM, NVDIMM or NVMEM battery). On AFF A700, AFF/ASA A900 and FAS9000/FAS9500 systems the battery sits in the DCPM (destage controller power module), which is hot-swapped.

name: Replace the NVRAM module or NVDIMM
description: Replace a failed NVRAM module or NVDIMM in a storage controller.

name: Replace the real-time clock battery
description: Shut down the impaired controller, replace the RTC battery, reinstall the controller module and reset the system time and date.

name: Replace the real-time clock battery in a shelf NSM
description: Replace the real-time clock battery inside an NVMe shelf module.

name: Restore and verify the system configuration after a controller replacement
description: After replacing a controller, check and correct the system time and the HA configuration state of the controller and chassis in Maintenance mode, then verify the disk list.

name: Shut down an existing controller module
description: The existing controller is halted and powered off so hardware can be added.

name: Shut down the controllers for chassis replacement
description: Client access and backups are stopped, AutoSupport case creation is suppressed, and the system's controllers are halted (or the impaired node is switched over in a two-node MetroCluster) so the chassis can be replaced safely.

name: Shut down the impaired controller
description: Shut down or take over the impaired controller before a hardware replacement.

name: Add a storage system to Virtual Storage Console
description: Register a storage cluster or SVM with Virtual Storage Console for VMware vSphere.

name: Apply ONTAP-level tags to block devices
description: ONTAP-level tags are applied automatically to block devices on EC2 hosts through a user data script, for resource management.

name: Bind iSCSI ports to the iSCSI software adapter
description: The ESXi host VMkernel iSCSI ports are bound to the iSCSI software adapter.

name: Complete host-side provisioning of SAN storage
description: After storage units are created and mapped, the host is zoned, discovers, initializes and formats them, and read/write access is verified.

name: Configure a host for FC and iSCSI with ONTAP storage
description: Configure a host operating system (Host Utilities, multipathing) to access ONTAP LUNs over FC or iSCSI.

name: Configure a host for NVMe-oF with ONTAP storage
description: Configure a host operating system (multipathing, NVMe initiator settings) to access ONTAP storage over NVMe-oF.

name: Configure a host to boot from an ONTAP SAN boot LUN
description: Set the host HBA BIOS or firmware boot device to the ONTAP SAN boot LUN, reboot, and verify that the host boots from it and sees its paths.

name: Configure DM-Multipath on a Linux host
description: DM-Multipath is configured, started and enabled at boot on a Linux host so that ONTAP LUN paths are managed.

name: Configure ESXi host best practice settings
description: The NetApp recommended multipath, HBA and NFS settings are applied to an ESXi host.

name: Configure ESXi host ports and vSwitches for NFS
description: VMkernel ports and a standard vSwitch are configured on an ESXi host for NFS datastore traffic.

name: Configure host iSCSI ports and vSwitches
description: VMkernel iSCSI ports and a vSphere standard switch are created on the ESXi host for iSCSI traffic.

name: Configure SAN booting on a host
description: Map a boot LUN to the host, enable SAN boot in the server BIOS and verify the host boots from it.

name: Configure SMB server options for Hyper-V and SQL Server
description: The SMB server options required for nondisruptive Hyper-V and SQL Server over SMB operations are verified and enabled.

name: Configure the VSS shadow copy directory depth
description: The directory depth for VSS shadow copies on Hyper-V over SMB shares is set.

name: Create a continuously available SMB share
description: Continuously available SMB shares are created for Hyper-V or SQL Server application servers to support nondisruptive operations.

name: Create a file system on a LUN on the host
description: A newly discovered LUN is initialized, partitioned or placed under logical volume management, and formatted with a file system on the host.

name: Create an NFS datastore for VMware
description: Provision an ONTAP volume and mount it as an NFS datastore on VMware ESXi hosts.

name: Discover LUNs on a host
description: Rescan on the host to discover newly mapped ONTAP LUNs and their multipath devices, and check path priorities.

name: Enable CAW on an ESXi datastore
description: Enable Compare and Write (ATS) on a transitioned VMFS datastore using the ESXi CLI.

name: Enable multipathing for NVMe devices on a host
description: Add the NVMe device ID to the host MPIO configuration so NVMe namespaces are multipathed.

name: Enable NVMe deallocate on an ESXi host
description: The NVMe DSM deallocate setting is enabled on an ESXi host so that space reclamation works with ONTAP NVMe namespaces.

name: Enable NVMe/FC on a host HBA
description: Set the host FC HBA driver parameters so the adapter supports NVMe/FC.

name: Enable or disable VMware vStorage over NFS
description: VMware vStorage APIs for Array Integration support over NFS is turned on or off for an SVM.

name: Enable or disable VSS shadow copies for Hyper-V over SMB backups
description: Turns VSS shadow copy support for Hyper-V over SMB backups on or off.

name: Enable the iSCSI software adapter
description: The iSCSI software adapter is enabled on the ESXi host.

name: Gather pretransition host information from the Inventory Assessment Workbook
description: The LUN names and host details needed for transition are identified and recorded from the Inventory Assessment Workbook.

name: Install host utilities on a SAN host
description: Install NetApp Host Utilities (AIX, HP-UX, Linux, Solaris, Windows) on a SAN host connected to ONTAP storage.

name: Install the HBA vendor utility
description: The HBA vendor management utility is installed on the SAN host.

name: Install the NFS Plug-in for VMware VAAI
description: The NetApp NFS Plug-in for VMware VAAI is installed on ESXi hosts so that they can offload NFS operations to the storage system.

name: Install Virtual Storage Console
description: Download and deploy the Virtual Storage Console virtual appliance.

name: Migrate an Oracle database by host filesystem copy
description: Move Oracle database files to ONTAP storage by copying them from one host filesystem to another with rsync.

name: Modify the HBA queue depth on a SAN host
description: The HBA or device queue depth on a SAN host is changed to a value appropriate for the ONTAP configuration.

name: Mount datastores on hosts
description: Existing datastores are mounted on additional ESXi hosts.

name: Mount transitioned LUNs with file systems on a host
description: After a 7-Mode transition, discover the new ONTAP LUNs on the host and remount their file systems, volume groups, disk sets, zpools or VMFS datastores.

name: Prepare AIX hosts for SnapMirror active sync
description: AIX host storage units are configured with the access mode and host settings required before SnapMirror active sync protection.

name: Prepare an ESXi host for post-transition remediation
description: Generate the LUN mapping file and verify igroups, zoning and volume rehosting before remediating ESXi hosts after transition.

name: Prepare ESXi hosts for transition
description: Gather host information, complete zoning and check interoperability before transitioning ESXi hosts.

name: Prepare Linux guest operating systems for transition
description: Update device references in Linux guest operating systems on ESXi to UUIDs before transition.

name: Prepare SAN boot LUNs for transition
description: Before a 7-Mode transition, identify and record the host's SAN boot LUN devices, WWIDs and boot configuration.

name: Prepare SAN host data LUNs for transition
description: Host-side information and configuration for data LUNs (devices, volume groups, pools, mount points) are recorded and adjusted so the LUNs can be transitioned.

name: Provision a datastore with its LUN and volume
description: A VMware datastore is provisioned from the vSphere client together with its containing ONTAP volume and LUN.

name: Provision Microsoft SQL Server storage over SAN
description: Add a Microsoft SQL Server instance application so the storage for its databases and logs is provisioned over SAN.

name: Re-register VMs on ESXi hosts after transition
description: The VMs on non-SAN-boot ESXi hosts are registered again from their configuration files after transition.

name: Reattach RDM LUNs to VMs after transition
description: After a 7-Mode transition, remove the stale raw device mappings and reattach the transitioned LUNs to their ESXi virtual machines as RDMs, using the vSphere Client or the ESXi CLI.

name: Record the host iSCSI initiator node name
description: The host iSCSI initiator node name is recorded so it can be added to an igroup.

name: Record the WWPNs of host FC ports
description: Record the WWPN of every host FC HBA port for use in switch zoning and igroup creation.

name: Remove VM snapshots before transition
description: Snapshots of ESXi virtual machines are deleted before transition.

name: Repair or remove the Host Utilities
description: The Windows Host Utilities installation on a host is repaired or uninstalled.

name: Replace 7-Mode LUN WWIDs on a Linux host after transition
description: Update DMMP devices without file systems on a Linux host to use the new ONTAP LUN WWIDs after transition.

name: Roll back transitioned LUNs to 7-Mode LUNs on a host
description: Reconfigure a host to use its original 7-Mode LUNs instead of the transitioned ONTAP LUNs.

name: Set the iSCSI replacement timeout on a Linux host
description: The iSCSI session replacement timeout on the Linux host is changed from its default to the recommended value.

name: Start iSCSI sessions from a host to the target
description: From the host, discover the ONTAP iSCSI target (by its IQN or portals) and log in to create iSCSI sessions so the host can reach the LUN.

name: Start the iSCSI service on the host
description: The iSCSI initiator service is started on the Linux host.

name: Test iSCSI paths from the host to the storage cluster
description: Network connectivity from the host to every iSCSI LIF in the cluster is verified.

name: Test transitioned data LUNs on a host before transition cutover
description: Before the cutover phase of a copy-based 7-Mode transition, map the transitioned data LUNs to a test host and verify the host and its applications can access them.

name: Update the HBA driver, firmware, and BIOS on an ESXi host
description: Check and update the FC HBA driver, firmware and BIOS on an ESXi host to supported versions.

name: Upgrade Windows Host Utilities
description: The Windows Host Utilities on the host are upgraded to a newer version.

name: Verify continuously available SMB share configuration
description: The SMB shares used by Hyper-V or SQL Server are confirmed to be continuously available with the required share settings.

name: Verify FC HBA driver settings set by the Host Utilities
description: The FC HBA driver parameters that the Host Utilities changed on the host are reviewed in the HBA vendor management tool.

name: Verify NFS access from an ESXi host
description: A virtual machine is created on the NFS datastore from the ESXi host to confirm NFS access works.

name: Verify RHEL DMMP devices without file systems are ready for transition
description: RHEL DMMP devices with no file system are confirmed ready to transition.

name: Verify that a host can read from and write to a LUN
description: Write data to a newly provisioned LUN or multipath device from the host and read it back, optionally across a storage failover.

name: Verify that an ESXi NFS configuration is supported
description: The combination of ONTAP, ESXi, VSC and plug-in versions is confirmed as supported in the Interoperability Matrix.

name: Verify the NVMe/FC configuration on a host
description: Confirm that the host NVMe/FC adapters, subsystems, namespaces and ANA paths are correctly discovered.

name: Verify the NVMe/TCP configuration on a host
description: Confirm that the host NVMe/TCP adapter, connections and namespace paths are correctly established.

name: Acquire a Capacity Pool license
description: Obtains an ONTAP Select Capacity Pool license file from the NetApp Support site.

name: Acquire an ONTAP Select Capacity Tier license
description: Generates an ONTAP Select Capacity Tier license file from the NetApp license site.

name: Acquire port licenses on an FC switch
description: Port licenses on a Cisco FC switch are released from unused ports and acquired for the ports used by the MetroCluster configuration.

name: Convert a node-based license to a capacity-based license
description: A Cloud Volumes ONTAP system's node-based license is converted to a capacity-based charging method.

name: Convert an evaluation license to a production license
description: Changes a cluster's evaluation license into an available production license in the Deploy utility.

name: Delete a license
description: Delete one or more installed licenses from the cluster.

name: Download NetApp license files
description: Gets the NetApp License Files for a system's serial number from the NetApp Support Site.

name: Install a license
description: Add license keys or NetApp License Files to the cluster to enable ONTAP features such as FC, iSCSI, FabricPool or SnapMirror, after checking which licenses are already installed.

name: Install switch port licenses
description: Install license files on a cluster switch to enable additional ports and verify that the new ports are available.

name: Modify the license manager configuration
description: Updates the cluster's existing license manager instance.

name: Register a pay-as-you-go Cloud Volumes ONTAP system
description: Register a pay-as-you-go Cloud Volumes ONTAP system with NetApp support using a NetApp Support Site account.

name: Reinstall capacity pool licenses on a new Deploy instance
description: Capacity pool licenses from a lost Deploy instance are reissued and installed on a new Deploy instance and the nodes are updated to use it.

name: Set the preferred billing subscription for Cloud Volumes ONTAP
description: Configure a standalone marketplace listing as the preferred billing subscription for Cloud Volumes ONTAP in the NetApp Console.

name: Set up licensing for Cloud Volumes ONTAP
description: Obtain and prepare the chosen licensing option (BYOL, annual contract, Freemium, Keystone or PAYGO subscription) so it can be selected when adding a Cloud Volumes ONTAP system.

name: Verify FC switch license requirements
description: The licenses a MetroCluster configuration needs are confirmed to be installed on the FC switches.

name: Verify licenses on replaced nodes
description: Licenses on replaced nodes are checked after switchback and replacement keys are installed and stale licenses cleaned up as needed.

name: View capacity pool licenses
description: Display the capacity pool licenses associated with the cluster and their node assignments.

name: View capacity tier licenses
description: The capacity tier licenses and their details are shown.

name: View licenses
description: Display the licenses installed on an ONTAP cluster, or the details of a specific license package.

name: View the license manager configuration
description: Gets information about the license manager instance associated with the cluster.

name: Acknowledge a risk
description: Acknowledge an open risk with a comment.

name: Acknowledge system health alerts
description: Marks a system health alert as acknowledged, under the administrator's name.

name: Add a cluster to Active IQ Unified Manager
description: A cluster is added as a data source so Active IQ Unified Manager monitors it.

name: Add an alert in Unified Manager
description: Define an Active IQ Unified Manager alert that selects the resources and events that trigger it, the recipients to notify and the notification frequency.

name: Add an SNMP traphost
description: Configure a traphost to receive SNMP event notifications from the cluster.

name: Add FC switches to health monitoring
description: The MetroCluster FC switches are added to ONTAP health monitoring by IP address and verified.

name: Add FC-to-SAS bridges to health monitoring
description: FC-to-SAS bridges are added to ONTAP health monitoring so their status is reported by the cluster.

name: Analyze volume performance trends
description: Weekly and monthly historical latency data for a volume is reviewed to find out whether it is underused or overused.

name: Apply an adaptive QoS policy group
description: An adaptive QoS policy group is created and applied to a volume so that its throughput limits scale with the volume size.

name: Assign a QoS policy group to a LUN
description: Set or change the QoS policy group applied to a LUN.

name: Assign a QoS policy to a file
description: A QoS policy is assigned to a file.

name: Assign a QoS policy to a volume
description: Set or change the Storage QoS policy group applied to an existing volume.

name: Assign an adaptive QoS policy group template to an SVM
description: An adaptive QoS policy group template is set on an SVM so its volumes inherit adaptive QoS.

name: Check disk throughput and latency
description: Displays disk throughput and latency statistics to identify disk-level performance problems.

name: Check SMB multiplex settings
description: The SMB maximum multiplex setting is checked and modified to correct slow SMB network performance.

name: Check throughput and latency between nodes
description: Network throughput and latency between cluster nodes are measured to check the infrastructure.

name: Configure automatic system health alert notifications
description: Defines an event destination and routes health monitor alert messages to it, so that system health alerts arrive automatically.

name: Configure EMS event notifications to an external destination
description: Forward important EMS events to an external receiver (email, syslog server or webhook) by creating a notification destination and an event notification that links a filter such as important-events to it.

name: Configure log collection for switch health monitoring
description: Set up and enable periodic and support log collection from cluster and storage switches through Ethernet switch health monitoring.

name: Configure SNMP settings for the MetroCluster Tiebreaker software
description: Configure SNMP settings in the Tiebreaker software so it sends SNMP notifications.

name: Configure SNMPv3 for switch health monitoring
description: Create an SNMPv3 user on the switch and a matching SNMP login in ONTAP so the ONTAP switch health monitor can poll the switch over SNMPv3.

name: Configure system-wide EMS email parameters
description: The system-wide email parameters used by EMS event notifications are set.

name: Configure the low spare disk warning threshold
description: Sets the minimum number of hot spare drives below which low-spare warnings are issued.

name: Create a QoS policy group
description: Create a QoS policy group for an SVM with throughput limits.

name: Create an application log event
description: A new app.log EMS event is generated from an application.

name: Create an EMS event filter
description: Creates an EMS event filter whose rules select events by matching criteria.

name: Create an EMS filter rule
description: Add a new rule to an existing EMS event filter.

name: Create an event notification destination
description: Add a destination, such as an email address, syslog server or webhook, that receives EMS event notifications.

name: Create an SNMP community
description: Create an SNMPv1/v2c community for the cluster or SVM.

name: Create an SNMPv3 user
description: Create a local or remote SNMPv3 security user with authentication and privacy settings on an ONTAP cluster.

name: Customize insights settings
description: Choose which system insights are evaluated and shown by the management GUI.

name: Delete a QoS policy group
description: Delete an existing QoS policy group.

name: Delete an EMS event filter
description: Removes an EMS event filter.

name: Delete an EMS event notification destination
description: Removes an EMS event notification destination.

name: Delete an EMS filter rule
description: Remove a rule from an existing event filter.

name: Delete an SNMP traphost
description: Removes an SNMP traphost from the cluster.

name: Delete an SNMP user
description: Removes an SNMP user from the cluster.

name: Delete system health alerts
description: Removes a system health alert.

name: Deploy Active IQ Unified Manager
description: Download the Unified Manager OVA from the NetApp Support Site and deploy it as a virtual appliance in VMware vSphere.

name: Determine whether to modify a Flash Pool caching policy
description: Volume workload pattern and cache hit rates are analysed to decide whether the Flash Pool caching policy should be changed.

name: Disable extended performance monitoring on a qtree
description: Turn off extended performance statistics collection for a qtree.

name: Disable SNMP
description: Turn off the SNMP protocol for the cluster.

name: Disable the SNMP trap subsystem
description: Disable SNMP traps cluster-wide so the cluster stops sending them.

name: Dismiss a configuration analysis
description: A best-practice configuration analysis that does not apply is dismissed for a file system.

name: Enable activity tracking on volumes
description: File System Analytics activity tracking is turned on for one or more volumes.

name: Enable extended performance monitoring on a qtree
description: Turn on extended performance statistics collection for a qtree.

name: Enable File System Analytics on a volume
description: Turn on File System Analytics (usage analytics) for a volume.

name: Enable or disable Flash Cache modules
description: Turn hardware Flash Cache modules on or off per node.

name: Enable or disable SNMP
description: Turn the SNMP protocol on (or off) for the cluster.

name: Enable or disable SNMP traps
description: Turn SNMP traps on or off for configured trap hosts.

name: Enable or disable throughput floors v2
description: Throughput floors v2 is turned on or off so that QoS floors are or are not met under heavy controller load.

name: Enable SNMP authentication traps
description: SNMP authentication traps are enabled for the cluster, optionally together with the SNMP protocol.

name: Export system insights to a PDF file
description: The System Manager insights page is exported as a PDF file.

name: Fix a configuration issue
description: A reported configuration issue is fixed by applying the recommended best-practice configuration.

name: Identify high-traffic clients and files
description: Lists the clients and files that access the cluster most.

name: Identify hot volumes
description: Sorts and filters volumes by IOPS, latency and throughput to find the volumes and other objects accessed most.

name: Install the Ethernet switch health monitor configuration file
description: Download and install the CSHM configuration file so that ONTAP can monitor the health of a cluster or storage switch.

name: Link the cluster to a Digital Advisor account
description: Register the management GUI with Digital Advisor to monitor system risks.

name: Modify a QoS policy group
description: Change the throughput limits or settings of an existing QoS policy group.

name: Modify a switch IP address for MetroCluster health monitoring
description: Replace the switch entries registered for health monitoring with their new IP addresses.

name: Modify administrative audit settings for GET requests
description: The audit log records or stops recording GET requests from the selected management interfaces.

name: Modify an EMS event filter
description: Changes an existing EMS event filter, for example by adding a rule.

name: Modify an EMS event notification destination
description: Updates an existing EMS event notification destination, for example its email address.

name: Modify an EMS filter rule
description: Update an existing event filter rule, such as changing its severity match.

name: Modify an SNMP user
description: The properties of an SNMP user, such as its comment, are updated.

name: Modify cluster SNMP settings
description: Change cluster-wide SNMP information such as contact and location.

name: Modify default File System Analytics settings
description: The SVMs on which new volumes get Activity Tracking and File System Analytics by default are set.

name: Modify QoS options
description: Cluster QoS options such as the background task reservation percentage are updated.

name: Modify the Flash Pool caching policy of a volume
description: Changes which read and write data of a volume are cached in the Flash Pool SSD cache.

name: Modify the IP address of an ATTO bridge for health monitoring
description: Bridge entries with old IP addresses are removed from health monitoring and added again with their new addresses.

name: Modify the iSCSI TCP window size
description: The iSCSI TCP read/write window size of an SVM is checked and changed if necessary.

name: Monitor FPolicy performance counters
description: Collects and displays FPolicy performance counters to monitor FPolicy server and policy performance.

name: Monitor network port health
description: Port health monitors are enabled or disabled for an IPspace and the detailed health of network ports is viewed.

name: Monitor storage unit performance
description: View and download latency, IOPS and throughput data for a storage unit.

name: Perform daily performance monitoring
description: Reviews the active performance events in Unified Manager each day and decides what action each event needs.

name: Reactivate a dismissed configuration analysis
description: A dismissed configuration analysis is active and evaluated again.

name: Respond to insights
description: Act on system insights, such as fixing or dismissing them, to optimize the system.

name: Set a throughput ceiling with a QoS policy group
description: Create a fixed QoS policy group with a maximum throughput, apply it to a storage object such as a volume, LUN, file or SVM, and monitor its performance.

name: Set a throughput floor with a QoS policy group
description: A QoS policy group with a minimum throughput is created and applied to a volume or LUN to guarantee its throughput.

name: Set performance event thresholds
description: Warning and critical performance threshold policies are created and assigned to storage objects so that events are raised when the thresholds are crossed.

name: Set the Flash Pool cache-retention policy for a volume
description: Changes how long a volume's data is retained in the Flash Pool cache.

name: Set volume latency thresholds
description: Sets latency thresholds on a volume so that performance alerts are raised when they are exceeded.

name: Suppress system health alerts
description: Suppresses a system health alert so that it no longer generates notifications.

name: Test cloud tier latency and throughput
description: Runs the object store profiler to measure latency and throughput to a cloud tier before attaching it.

name: Test SNMP polling
description: Send an SNMP request from another host to confirm the cluster answers SNMP polls.

name: Test SNMP traps
description: Generate a test SNMP trap and confirm the configured traphosts receive it.

name: Troubleshoot a performance event
description: A performance event raised against a system-defined or user-defined threshold is analyzed and the suggested corrective actions are applied.

name: Unacknowledge a risk
description: Return a previously acknowledged risk to the open state.

name: Update EMS event mapping from deprecated commands
description: Replaces event destinations and routes made with the deprecated commands with event notification destinations, filters and notifications.

name: Verify cluster and storage health
description: Verify that cluster nodes, HA and storage are healthy.

name: Verify network settings on data switches
description: Checks that the data switches have an MTU size suitable for the cluster's data network.

name: Verify ONTAP Mediator service status
description: The ONTAP Mediator service status and the ports it listens on are checked to confirm it is running and healthy.

name: Verify that SNMP is enabled
description: Check that SNMP is enabled on the cluster.

name: Verify the health of a MetroCluster configuration
description: Run the MetroCluster diagnostic checks and review their results (overall and per component such as nodes, aggregates, LIFs and volumes) to confirm the MetroCluster configuration is healthy.

name: Verify the MTU setting of network ports
description: The storage system's port MTU is checked against clients and network endpoints and changed on the broadcast domain if it does not match.

name: View a storage overview
description: Display an overview of the storage system's data containers such as volumes and buckets.

name: View Active IQ risks
description: View the number and details of Active IQ risks reported for the cluster.

name: View administrative audit settings for GET requests
description: The settings that control whether GET requests from each management interface are recorded in the audit log are displayed.

name: View available statistics objects and counters
description: The statistics objects and counters available for SMB monitoring are listed.

name: View BranchCache statistics
description: BranchCache-related counters are collected and displayed for the SMB server.

name: View cluster events and jobs
description: Cluster events and jobs are reviewed in System Manager.

name: View cluster performance
description: View cluster performance metrics such as latency, IOPS and throughput.

name: View connected NAS clients
description: Display the NFS (and SMB) clients currently connected to the cluster in System Manager.

name: View consistency group metrics
description: Retrieve historical performance and space metrics for a consistency group over a time range.

name: View DNS statistics for an SVM
description: DNS performance counters for an SVM are sampled and displayed.

name: View EMS event destinations
description: Retrieve EMS event notification destinations and their details, including their connectivity test status.

name: View EMS event filters
description: Retrieve EMS event filters.

name: View EMS events
description: List and review EMS events generated by the ONTAP system.

name: View EMS filter rules
description: Retrieve the rules attached to an EMS event filter.

name: View environmental sensors
description: Show the readings and state of a node's environmental sensors, such as type, name, state, value and threshold warnings.

name: View File System Analytics data for a volume
description: Show File System Analytics capacity data for a volume's directory tree, such as the largest directories and subdirectories and histograms of data age.

name: View file-directory security policy jobs
description: The progress and status of security policy jobs applied to the SVM are displayed.

name: View Insights recommendations
description: Review the System Manager Insights recommendations for optimizing cluster security, capacity and performance.

name: View job status
description: View cluster jobs and monitor their status and progress.

name: View LDAP statistics
description: LDAP performance counters for an SVM are displayed.

name: View MetroCluster configurations monitored by Tiebreaker
description: Display the MetroCluster configurations (monitors) in the Tiebreaker software with their cluster addresses, monitoring status, operation history and statistics.

name: View MetroCluster operations
description: The list of MetroCluster operations, or the details of a specific operation, is retrieved.

name: View NFS statistics
description: NFS performance statistics for an SVM are collected and displayed.

name: View NFSv4 storepool resource consumption
description: The NFSv4 storepool resources used by clients are displayed.

name: View NIS statistics
description: NIS performance statistics for an SVM are collected and displayed.

name: View nondisruptive operation status
description: Use system health monitoring to display the NDO health status and CIFS-NDO alert configuration.

name: View ONTAP Select Deploy event messages
description: Display and optionally filter the event messages logged by the ONTAP Select Deploy utility.

name: View performance counter tables
description: Query cluster performance counter tables, their schema definitions, rows and counters.

name: View QoS options
description: Retrieve the cluster-wide QoS options.

name: View QoS workloads
description: List the QoS workloads on the cluster, or show the details of one.

name: View qtree performance statistics
description: Shows performance metrics for a qtree with extended performance monitoring enabled.

name: View remaining performance capacity
description: Collects and displays real-time headroom statistics to identify remaining performance capacity on nodes and local tiers.

name: View SMB statistics
description: Collects and displays CIFS/SMB statistics counters, such as encryption, signing, and automatic node referral activity, to monitor SMB performance and behaviour.

name: View SNMP traphosts
description: List SNMP traphosts configured in the cluster or display a specific traphost.

name: View SNMP users
description: Lists the SNMP users in the cluster, or gets the details of one SNMP user.

name: View storage availability zone capacity
description: Monitor the capacity utilization of the cluster's storage availability zones.

name: View tape backup and restore event logs
description: Open the event log files that record tape backup and restore operations from the nodeshell.

name: View the cluster dashboard
description: The System Manager dashboard showing cluster health, capacity and performance is reviewed.

name: View the EMS configuration
description: Gets the cluster's current EMS configuration, such as the mail server settings.

name: View the status of operations
description: The progress and status of management operations are shown and filtered in Tracker, and can be downloaded.

name: View the status of the ONTAP Select Deploy mediator service
description: Display the status of the mediator service that monitors two-node clusters from the Deploy utility.

name: View top clients by I/O activity
description: Retrieve the clients with the most read/write activity for a volume or SVM.

name: View top directories by I/O activity
description: Retrieve the directories with the most read/write traffic for a volume or SVM.

name: View top files by I/O activity
description: Retrieve the files with the most read/write traffic for a volume or SVM.

name: View top users by I/O activity
description: Retrieve the users with the most read/write activity for a volume or SVM.

name: View Vscan event log
description: Vscan event log entries for the SVM are displayed.

name: View Vscan server statistics
description: Statistics on Vscan server requests, latencies and utilization are collected and displayed.

name: Add a port to an interface group
description: Adds a physical network port to an existing interface group (LAG).

name: Add an Ethernet switch for monitoring
description: Add a cluster or storage Ethernet switch so that ONTAP monitors it.

name: Add ISLs to an FC switch
description: New ISL ports are added, cabled, configured, and enabled on the FC switches of a MetroCluster fabric.

name: Add or remove a LIF in a DNS load balancing zone
description: Adds a LIF to or removes a LIF from a DNS load balancing zone.

name: Add or replace cluster switches for expansion
description: Add or replace cluster switches so the cluster network has enough ports for the planned expansion.

name: Add, remove, or change ISL ports on MetroCluster IP switches
description: Nondisruptively add, remove or change the ISL ports between MetroCluster IP switches.

name: Add, remove, or reassign ports in a broadcast domain
description: Change which network ports belong to a broadcast domain, including moving a port from its current broadcast domain to a different one.

name: Assess networking requirements before configuring client protocol access
description: Check available ports, subnets, IPspaces and IPv6 settings to confirm the network can support NFS, SMB or S3 client access before configuring it.

name: Assign a service policy to a LIF
description: Sets or changes the service policy used by a LIF, either at creation or on an existing interface.

name: Assign buffer-to-buffer credits to F-ports sharing a port group with an ISL
description: Buffer-to-buffer credits on F-ports that share a port group with the ISL are reduced so the ISL can use the rest.

name: Bring a MetroCluster IP interface port online or offline
description: A MetroCluster IP interconnect port is taken offline or brought back online from the ONTAP CLI.

name: Change ISL properties and IOD/OOD configuration on an FC switch
description: Change inter-switch link properties such as port speed, distance, or in-order/out-of-order delivery on a MetroCluster FC switch.

name: Change the personality of a unified target adapter port
description: Use ucadmin to change a UTA/UTA2 port's mode (CNA/Ethernet or FC) and its FC target/initiator type.

name: Configure a node management LIF
description: Create and configure the node management LIF (and related service processor settings) for a node.

name: Configure and connect MetroCluster IP interfaces
description: MetroCluster IP interfaces are created on every node and connected so the DR partners can communicate.

name: Configure basic settings on MetroCluster FC switches
description: Basic switch parameters are set on each FC switch, such as the domain, routing policy, virtual fabrics and SNMP community string.

name: Configure cluster ports and cluster LIFs on a controller module
description: Ports are given the cluster role, LIFs homed on them are moved elsewhere, and cluster LIFs are created on the new cluster ports.

name: Configure compression on FC switch ISL ports
description: Compression is turned on for the ISL ports of the FC switches, and the setting is confirmed.

name: Configure DNS for an SVM
description: Create a DNS configuration (domains and name servers) on an SVM, or at cluster scope, so that it can resolve host names.

name: Configure dynamic DNS on an SVM
description: Enable, disable or change dynamic DNS (DDNS) settings on an SVM so its LIF records are updated automatically in DNS.

name: Configure E-ports on MetroCluster FC switches
description: The ISL E-ports on each FC switch are configured with port speed, trunking, QoS, distance and buffer-to-buffer credits.

name: Configure F-ports on an FC switch
description: Switch ports on a Cisco FC switch in a MetroCluster FC fabric are set to F mode for controller and bridge connections.

name: Configure FC-VI ports on a quad-port FC adapter
description: Ports on a quad-port FC adapter are disabled and changed to FC-VI mode for MetroCluster FC interconnect use.

name: Configure FCIP ISL ports on MetroCluster FC switches
description: Configure the FCIP ports (IP interfaces, tunnels/profiles and circuits) on the MetroCluster FC switches so that the fabric ISLs run over IP.

name: Configure in-order or out-of-order frame delivery in ONTAP
description: ONTAP is configured for in-order or out-of-order delivery of frames on the MetroCluster FC interconnect adapters.

name: Configure iSCSI LIFs to return FQDN for SendTargets discovery
description: iSCSI LIFs are set to return their fully qualified domain name to hosts during SendTargets discovery.

name: Configure LIF failover settings
description: The failover group and failover policy of an existing LIF are set.

name: Configure MetroCluster IP switches
description: Configure the IP switches of a MetroCluster IP configuration (RCF, port speeds, unused ISL ports) for new or replacement switches.

name: Configure switch ports for copper cable connections
description: Configure switch ports that use 40GbE/100GbE copper cables so that the links come up.

name: Configure the CDP advertisement interval
description: The interval for sending CDP advertisements is set on the ports of a node or all nodes.

name: Configure the CDP hold time
description: The hold time for CDP messages is set on all ports of a node or of all nodes in the cluster.

name: Configure the host storage network for best performance
description: Maximizes iSCSI/NFS network performance by using dedicated high-speed ports on the same network, disabling flow control and enabling jumbo frames.

name: Configure the LLDP advertisement interval
description: The interval for transmitting LLDP advertisements is set on the ports of a node or all nodes.

name: Configure the network for NFS trunking
description: Failover groups and additional LIFs on the same node are set up so NFS clients can use trunked connections.

name: Configure the timeout for dynamic routes from ICMP redirects
description: The ICMP/ICMPv6 redirect timeout is modified so that dynamic routes are removed from routing tables after the specified time.

name: Configure TLS hardware offload
description: TLS hardware offload is enabled or disabled on the cluster.

name: Configure zoning on MetroCluster FC switches
description: Create and activate the FC zones on the switches of a MetroCluster FC configuration (Brocade or Cisco).

name: Convert 40GbE NIC ports into 10GbE ports
description: A 40GbE network interface card is converted in maintenance mode to provide four 10GbE ports and recabled for 10GbE connectivity.

name: Convert management LIFs from IPv4 to IPv6
description: IPv6 management LIFs replace the IPv4 management LIFs on the cluster.

name: Create a BGP peer group
description: A BGP peer group is created to establish BGP sessions with a remote router, using either an existing or a newly provisioned local interface.

name: Create a broadcast domain
description: A new broadcast domain is created in an IPspace with a name, MTU and member ports.

name: Create a cluster management LIF
description: A cluster management LIF is created with an IP address and port.

name: Create a DNS load balancing zone
description: Create a DNS load balancing zone by assigning data LIFs to a DNS zone so client DNS requests are distributed across LIFs.

name: Create a failover group
description: A failover group listing the ports a LIF can fail over to is created for an SVM.

name: Create a LIF
description: Create an IP data network interface (LIF) on an SVM with a home node, port, address, and a service policy or data protocol (for example NFS, SMB, iSCSI or S3) and failover settings.

name: Create a LIF service policy
description: Create a custom network service policy, cluster- or SVM-scoped, that defines which services (for example data-iscsi or data-s3-server) LIFs using it support.

name: Create a local hosts table entry
description: Add a local hostname-to-IP mapping entry for an SVM.

name: Create a static route
description: Create a cluster-scoped or SVM-scoped static route.

name: Create a subnet
description: Create an IP subnet with an IP address range for LIF provisioning.

name: Create a virtual IP data LIF
description: Creates a virtual IP data LIF advertised through BGP and verifies that the SVM's BGP session is up.

name: Create a VLAN
description: Creates a tagged VLAN port on a physical port or interface group, optionally in a specific broadcast domain.

name: Create an FC LIF
description: An FC network interface is created on a specified FC port of a node.

name: Create an HTTP proxy configuration
description: Create an HTTP proxy configuration for an IPspace or an SVM, optionally with authentication.

name: Create an interface group
description: Create an interface group (LAG/ifgrp) port from physical Ethernet ports on a node, optionally in a specific broadcast domain.

name: Create an IPspace
description: Create an IPspace to provide a distinct IP address space for SVMs.

name: Create intercluster LIFs
description: Create intercluster LIFs on the nodes of a cluster, on dedicated or shared data ports, to enable cluster peering and cross-cluster replication traffic.

name: Create VSANs on MetroCluster FC switches
description: FC-VI and storage VSANs are created, given their member ports, and set for in-order delivery on the FC switches.

name: Delete a broadcast domain
description: A broadcast domain is removed from the cluster.

name: Delete a LIF
description: Delete a logical interface (LIF) from the cluster, first removing it from any port set if it serves SAN hosts.

name: Delete a service policy
description: Removes a network service policy from the cluster.

name: Delete a static route
description: Removes a static route from an SVM's routing table.

name: Delete a subnet
description: Delete an IP subnet.

name: Delete a VLAN
description: Delete a VLAN from a network port.

name: Delete an interface group
description: An interface group (LAG) is removed.

name: Delete an IPspace
description: Delete an IPspace that is no longer needed.

name: Disable automatic iSCSI LIF failover
description: Automatic failover is disabled for an iSCSI LIF.

name: Disable Azure Private Link for Cloud Volumes ONTAP
description: Turn off Azure Private Link so Cloud Volumes ONTAP connects to its storage accounts through service endpoints instead.

name: Enable automatic iSCSI LIF failover
description: Automatic failover is enabled for an iSCSI LIF.

name: Enable IP port access on an FC-to-SAS bridge
description: Access services on the bridge Ethernet ports are enabled through the serial console and the configuration is saved.

name: Enable IPv6 for SMB servers
description: Enables IPv6 on the cluster so SMB servers can serve clients and access services over IPv6.

name: Enable multipath routing
description: Enable multipath routing at advanced privilege so traffic is distributed across all available routes.

name: Enable or disable CDP
description: Turns Cisco Discovery Protocol on or off for all ports of a node or of all nodes in the cluster.

name: Enable or disable LLDP
description: Turns Link Layer Discovery Protocol on or off for all ports of a node or of all nodes in the cluster.

name: Enable rollback on Azure Private Link failures
description: Configure the Console agent to roll back Cloud Volumes ONTAP operations when Azure Private Link creation fails.

name: Enable the RACK TCP stack on an IPspace
description: The PRR/RACK TCP stack is enabled on an IPspace, and the change is confirmed, to improve TCP performance over the WAN.

name: Identify ports available for a broadcast domain
description: Determines which ports are free of LIF assignments and can be moved into a new broadcast domain.

name: Install RCF files on MetroCluster FC switches
description: The correct reference configuration files are downloaded and applied to each MetroCluster FC switch.

name: Install the reference configuration file on an Ethernet switch
description: Download or generate the NetApp reference configuration file (RCF) and apply it to a cluster, storage, shared or MetroCluster IP Ethernet switch so its ports and settings match the supported configuration.

name: Look up a host record
description: A hostname is resolved to an IP address, or an IP address to a hostname, using an SVM's name services.

name: Look up IP addresses for a DNS service name
description: Retrieve the service IP addresses that DNS resolves for a given service name, optionally filtered by IPv4 or IPv6 address type.

name: Map the SMB server on the DNS server
description: Forward, reverse and alias DNS records resolve the SMB server name and NetBIOS aliases to its data LIFs.

name: Merge broadcast domains
description: The ports of one broadcast domain are moved into another broadcast domain, combining them into one.

name: Migrate a LIF
description: One or all LIFs are moved to a different port, optionally permanently.

name: Modify a BGP peer group
description: Updates a BGP peer group, such as changing its peer router address or renaming it.

name: Modify a broadcast domain
description: A broadcast domain's attributes, such as its name or MTU, are changed so that the new MTU applies to all member ports including interface group ports.

name: Modify a DNS configuration
description: Change the DNS domains, name servers or optional settings such as timeout and attempts of an existing SVM or cluster DNS configuration.

name: Modify a LIF
description: Change the properties of an existing logical interface (LIF), such as its home port, address, admin status or auto-revert setting.

name: Modify a service policy
description: Update a network interface service policy, for example renaming it or adding or removing the services it allows, such as removing management-ems.

name: Modify a subnet
description: Change an IP subnet's properties, such as its name, gateway or IP address ranges, including adding or removing IP addresses from the subnet.

name: Modify a VLAN
description: Edit the settings of an existing VLAN, such as its MTU size.

name: Modify an interface group
description: The settings of an existing interface group are changed.

name: Modify Ethernet switch monitoring settings
description: Configure the monitoring settings of an Ethernet switch.

name: Modify host cache settings
description: Update the hosts name service cache settings of an SVM.

name: Modify network port attributes
description: Change the settings of a physical Ethernet network port, such as admin status, MTU, speed, duplex, autonegotiation or flow control.

name: Modify QoS marking values
description: Changes the DSCP value or enabled state of QoS marking for a protocol in an IPspace.

name: Modify the LLDP advertisement time-to-live
description: Adjusts the hold multiplier that sets the time-to-live of LLDP advertisements on a node's ports.

name: Move a broadcast domain to another IPspace
description: Move a broadcast domain into a different IPspace.

name: Move a SAN LIF
description: Take a SAN LIF offline, assign it a new home node and port, and bring it back online.

name: Move cluster LIFs before MetroCluster IP switch maintenance
description: Migrate cluster LIFs off a MetroCluster IP switch before changing its firmware, RCF or hardware.

name: Prepare the target cluster data network for a 7-Mode transition
description: VLANs, interface groups and any IPspaces the transitioned SVMs need are created on the target cluster nodes before a 7-Mode transition.

name: Re-create VLANs, interface groups and broadcast domains on the new node
description: VLANs, interface groups and broadcast domains of the original node are re-created on the new node.

name: Re-enable the FC switch fabric and verify operation
description: The FC switches are re-enabled and the switches, logged-in devices, and fabric MetroCluster operation are verified.

name: Reconfigure in-order delivery on an FC switch
description: In-order guarantee of exchanges is enabled for the MetroCluster VSAN on an FC switch.

name: Remove a NIC from a node
description: Delete the ports of a NIC and physically remove the card from a cluster node.

name: Remove a port from an interface group
description: Removes a physical network port from an existing interface group (LAG).

name: Remove an Ethernet switch
description: Remove an Ethernet switch from monitoring.

name: Rename a MetroCluster FC switch
description: The FC switches are disabled, renamed, rebooted and re-enabled, and the new names are checked in ONTAP.

name: Rename a MetroCluster IP switch
description: The IP switch is given a new host name and the running configuration is saved to startup.

name: Rename an IPspace
description: Changes the name of an existing IPspace.

name: Repair network port reachability
description: Fixes ports whose reachability is repairable by reassigning them to the correct broadcast domain.

name: Reset an Ethernet switch to factory defaults
description: Erase the configuration of a cluster, storage, or MetroCluster IP Ethernet switch to return it to factory defaults.

name: Reset MetroCluster FC switches to factory defaults
description: The zoning and configuration on each FC switch are cleared and the switch is returned to factory default settings.

name: Revert LIFs to their home ports
description: Enable data LIFs and return LIFs to their home ports, for example after an ONTAP upgrade or revert.

name: Segregate SnapMirror traffic onto a dedicated network interface
description: SnapMirror replication traffic is isolated on an additional NIC, IPspace and intercluster LIF.

name: Set forward error correction on 25-Gbps switch ports
description: Forward error correction is turned off on 25-Gbps MetroCluster IP switch ports connected to controller modules.

name: Set up an AWS transit gateway for a Cloud Volumes ONTAP HA pair
description: An AWS transit gateway and routes are set up so clients can reach the HA pair's floating IP addresses.

name: Set up BGP for virtual IP LIFs
description: BGP is configured for the cluster, including the BGP configuration, BGP LIFs and peer groups, so that virtual IP LIFs can be advertised to routers.

name: Split a broadcast domain
description: Selected ports of an existing broadcast domain are moved into a newly created broadcast domain.

name: Verify and restore LIF configuration in a MetroCluster configuration
description: Verify that LIFs are hosted on their proper home nodes and ports before switchback, and restore the LIF configuration where needed.

name: Verify LIF status
description: The SVM's LIFs are confirmed to be up on their home ports, and any that are not are reverted to their home ports.

name: Verify network connectivity among ONTAP Select nodes
description: Confirm network connectivity among the ONTAP Select nodes of a cluster.

name: Verify the LIF failover configuration before an ONTAP upgrade
description: Check that data LIFs have failover enabled with targets on other nodes before upgrading.

name: Verify the RCF configuration on cluster switches
description: Check cluster ports, switch RCF and HA interconnect RDMA status during a controller upgrade.

name: View active network connections
description: Display active network connections in a cluster, grouped by LIF, client or protocol.

name: View BGP peer groups
description: Retrieve BGP peer groups configured in the cluster.

name: View broadcast domains
description: View broadcast domains in the cluster.

name: View DNS configurations
description: Display the DNS domain and name server configuration, including status and advanced fields, for one or all SVMs.

name: View Ethernet switch ports
description: Retrieves the ports of the monitored cluster or storage Ethernet switches.

name: View Ethernet switches
description: Retrieve the list of monitored Ethernet switches or a specific switch.

name: View failover groups
description: Failover groups, their target ports and broadcast domains, and the failover settings used by LIFs are displayed.

name: View FC LIFs
description: Retrieve the FC network interfaces (FC LIFs) of the cluster or an SVM, or one specific FC interface, with their properties.

name: View host cache settings
description: Retrieve the hosts name-service cache settings for all SVMs or for a given SVM.

name: View HTTP proxy configurations
description: Retrieve HTTP proxy configurations for all IPspaces and SVMs or for a specific SVM.

name: View interface groups
description: Interface groups (LAG ports) in the cluster and their details are displayed.

name: View IPspaces
description: List the IPspaces in the cluster or retrieve a specific IPspace.

name: View LIF failover targets
description: The ports each LIF can fail over to are displayed.

name: View LIFs
description: Display the network interfaces (IP LIFs) in the cluster or an SVM and their attributes.

name: View LIFs in a load balancing zone
description: The LIFs in a DNS load balancing zone and their load balancing details are displayed.

name: View listening network connections
description: Shows each node's listening network connections.

name: View local hosts table entries
description: Display the local hostname-to-IP mappings in the DNS hosts table for all SVMs or a specific SVM and address.

name: View network neighbor devices
description: Information about CDP- or LLDP-compliant devices connected to the node ports is displayed.

name: View network port reachability
description: Shows the reachability status of network ports and determines whether any corrective action is needed.

name: View network ports
description: Displays information about the physical, LAG and other Ethernet ports in the cluster.

name: View or clear CDP statistics
description: Displays or resets the Cisco Discovery Protocol statistics for the ports of a node.

name: View or clear LLDP statistics
description: Displays or resets the Link Layer Discovery Protocol statistics for the ports of a node.

name: View QoS marking values
description: Displays the DSCP QoS marking values configured per protocol and IPspace.

name: View routes
description: Displays the static routes of SVMs and the cluster, their association with LIFs, and the installed active routes.

name: View service policies
description: Lists the network service policies in the cluster or shows the details of a specific one.

name: View subnets
description: List IP subnets in the cluster or display a specific subnet.

name: View VLANs
description: Displays information about VLAN ports and their tags and underlying ports.

name: Assign a snapshot policy to an S3 bucket
description: Set the snapshot policy of a new or existing S3 bucket so bucket snapshots are created on schedule.

name: Change the size of an S3 bucket
description: Increases or decreases the capacity of an existing S3 bucket.

name: Configure an S3 client application to access the ONTAP S3 server
description: An S3 client application is authenticated to the ONTAP S3 server with server name, CA certificate and user keys so it can access buckets.

name: Create an S3 access point for a volume
description: Creates and attaches an S3 access point to a volume so its data can be accessed over S3.

name: Create an S3 bucket
description: Create an ONTAP S3 bucket on an SVM, optionally with policies and lifecycle rules, through System Manager, AFX, the CLI or the REST API, including in MetroCluster configurations.

name: Create an S3 bucket lifecycle management rule
description: Creates a lifecycle rule that expires or deletes objects in an S3 bucket according to defined criteria.

name: Create an S3 group
description: Create an S3 user group on an SVM to control access to buckets.

name: Create an S3 NAS bucket
description: An S3 NAS bucket is created that maps an S3 bucket name to a NAS path so S3 clients can access NAS data.

name: Create an S3 object store server
description: An S3 object store server is created on an SVM, over HTTP or HTTPS, optionally with users and buckets in the same request.

name: Create an S3 object store server policy
description: Create an S3 object store server policy with access statements that control S3 access to resources on an SVM.

name: Create an S3 user
description: Create an S3 user on an SVM, optionally with a key expiration configuration or as an Active Directory user.

name: Create and install a server certificate on an S3-enabled SVM
description: Create an SVM CA, sign a server certificate with it and install it on the S3-enabled SVM for HTTPS access.

name: Delete an S3 bucket
description: An S3 bucket is removed from an SVM.

name: Delete an S3 bucket policy
description: The access policy of an S3 bucket is removed.

name: Delete an S3 bucket snapshot
description: Delete a snapshot of an ONTAP S3 bucket.

name: Delete an S3 group
description: An S3 group is removed from an SVM.

name: Delete an S3 policy
description: An S3 object store policy is removed from an SVM.

name: Delete an S3 server
description: Delete the S3 server configuration of an SVM.

name: Delete an S3 user
description: An S3 user is removed from an SVM.

name: Delete an S3 user access key

name: Delete CORS rules from an S3 bucket
description: Removes the cross-origin resource sharing rules configured on an S3 bucket.

name: Delete S3 access points for a volume
description: Removes S3 access points from a volume.

name: Disable the S3 server
description: The S3 server of an SVM is administratively disabled.

name: Enable LDAP or domain users to generate S3 access keys
description: Configure the name service switch, a custom REST role and an LDAP or domain user group so directory users can generate their own S3 access keys through the API.

name: Enable S3 access to NAS FlexCache volumes
description: Configures certificates, the S3 server and clients so that NAS FlexCache volumes can be accessed over S3.

name: Enable S3 client users to access NAS data
description: S3 users are mapped to NAS users and granted bucket policy permissions so they can access NAS data through S3.

name: Enable S3 protocol access to NAS data on an SVM
description: S3 is enabled on a NAS-configured SVM with an object store server, certificate and data LIFs so NAS data can be served over S3.

name: Modify an S3 bucket

name: Modify an S3 bucket policy
description: Update an S3 bucket's access policy by adding or changing statements that grant users or groups allowed actions on the bucket.

name: Modify an S3 group
description: The membership or policies of an existing S3 group are updated.

name: Modify an S3 policy
description: The statements of an existing S3 object store policy are updated.

name: Modify S3 access points for a volume
description: Edits the settings of S3 access points attached to a volume.

name: Regenerate S3 user access keys
description: Generate new access and secret keys for an S3 user on an SVM, either regenerating key 1 or key 2 or adding a second key, optionally with a key retention period.

name: Restore an S3 bucket from a snapshot
description: Restore an S3 bucket's contents from one of its bucket snapshots.

description: Browse a bucket snapshot from an S3 client and copy objects from it back into the bucket.

name: Set up the journal table infrastructure for S3 access points
description: The journal table infrastructure used by S3 access points on a volume is set up.

name: View S3 access points for a volume
description: Displays details of the S3 access points attached to a volume.

name: View S3 bucket snapshots

name: View S3 groups

name: View S3 policies

name: View S3 server configuration

name: View S3 users
description: Display the S3 users of an SVM and their configuration, including their access keys.

name: Apply a Legal Hold to WORM files
description: Begin or end a Legal Hold that retains WORM files indefinitely during litigation.

name: Apply an event-based retention policy
description: Create an event-based retention policy and apply it so files are retained for a set period after an event occurs.

name: Classify abnormal activity as a false positive
description: Record flagged ARP activity as a false positive, clear the suspect state and resume normal ransomware monitoring.

name: Classify abnormal activity as a ransomware attack
description: Mark flagged ARP activity as a potential ransomware attack, optionally generate an attack report, and proceed to recover data.

name: Commit a file to WORM manually
description: Commit a file on a SnapLock volume to WORM by making it read-only from a client.

name: Commit snapshots to WORM on a vault destination
description: Snapshots replicated to a SnapLock vault destination are locked in WORM state.

name: Complete the Chain of Custody verification for transitioned SnapLock volumes
description: Run the Chain of Custody verification on transitioned SnapLock volumes and download the report.

name: Configure ARP alert settings
description: Choose which ARP events, such as new file extensions detected or ransomware snapshots created, raise alerts for a volume.

name: Configure immutable files for a volume
description: Immutable file (WORM retention) settings are configured for a volume.

name: Create a locked snapshot
description: Create a snapshot manually with a SnapLock retention period so it is tamperproof until expiry.

name: Create a SnapLock aggregate
description: Create a SnapLock Compliance or Enterprise aggregate to host SnapLock volumes.

name: Create a SnapLock volume
description: Create a SnapLock (WORM) volume on a SnapLock aggregate.

name: Create a SnapLock-protected audit log
description: Configure an SVM to write SnapLock audit logs to a mounted SnapLock volume.

name: Create a snapshot locking policy
description: Create a snapshot policy whose schedules apply a locking retention period to the snapshots they create.

name: Create a volume with snapshot locking enabled
description: Create a new volume with tamperproof snapshot locking enabled.

name: Create a WORM appendable file
description: Create a WORM appendable file on a SnapLock volume so data can be appended while committed parts stay protected.

name: Create an S3 bucket with object locking
description: A new S3 bucket is created with object locking enabled so objects are protected from change or deletion.

name: Create WORM appendable files with volume append mode
description: Enable volume append mode on a SnapLock volume and create WORM appendable files.

name: Delete WORM files on an Enterprise SnapLock volume
description: Use privileged delete to remove WORM files before their retention expires on an Enterprise-mode SnapLock volume.

name: Disable automatic ARP enablement
description: Turn off the setting that automatically enables Autonomous Ransomware Protection on volumes (for example after an upgrade or before a revert).

description: Turn on Autonomous Ransomware Protection for a specific volume or storage unit so it starts learning or evaluating and then detecting attacks.

description: The SnapLock Compliance Clock is set to resynchronize with trusted NTP servers.

description: Enable ONTAP native FPolicy on storage VMs and volumes so that file operations on common ransomware file extensions are blocked.

description: Allow a SnapLock administrator to delete WORM files on a SnapLock Enterprise volume before their retention expires.
