name: Create an application
description: Define an application entity for tracking assets and chargeback.

name: Create an asset page widget using $this variables
description: A widget on an asset's customizable page uses $this variables to show data related to the current asset.

name: Delete a data source
description: A data source is removed from Insight.

name: Delete a performance policy
description: A performance policy is removed.

name: Delete a query
description: A saved query is removed.

name: Delete an annotation
description: An annotation is removed.

name: Delete an annotation rule
description: An annotation rule is removed.

name: Delete an application
description: An application is removed.

name: Enable performance data archiving
description: Insight archives performance data daily to a specified location.

name: Enable syslog logging
description: Enable the Syslog section in Admin > Notifications with the log server address (and optional port) and facility level, so Insight sends violation, performance alert and optionally audit messages to a syslog server.

name: Export a custom report as XML
description: A report specification is copied to the clipboard and saved as an XML file so the report can be backed up or reused.

name: Export Fibre Channel device identifications to a CSV file
description: Fibre Channel device identifications are exported to a CSV file.

name: Export IP device identifications to a CSV file
description: IP device identifications are exported to a CSV file.

name: Export query results to a CSV file
description: The results of a query are exported to a .CSV file.

name: Force an update of annotations for Data Warehouse
description: Force changed annotations to be pushed right away to the Data Warehouse, so that reports use them without waiting for the scheduled update.

name: Group and roll up data in a table widget
description: A dashboard table widget groups assets by an attribute and rolls up their metrics (for example, sum or average) per group.

name: Identify devices using device resolution
description: Unidentified devices in the environment are identified through auto resolution rules, manual identification and CSV import.

name: Identify devices using rule-assisted manual identification
description: Selected unidentified devices are resolved by running a chosen set or order of rules.

name: Import a custom report from XML
description: A saved report specification (XML) is pasted from the clipboard into the reporting tool and saved as a report, for example to restore custom reports after an upgrade.

name: Import annotation values
description: Annotation values are imported into Insight from a file.

name: Import Fibre Channel device identifications from a CSV file
description: Fibre Channel device identifications are loaded from a CSV file.

name: Import IP device identifications from a CSV file
description: IP device identifications are loaded from a CSV file.

name: Load the performance archive
description: Archived performance data is loaded back into the Insight server from the Restore section of Admin > Troubleshooting. This is typically done after restoring a backup or after an upgrade that restored only seven days of archive data.

name: Modify a performance policy
description: An existing performance policy's settings or thresholds are changed.

name: Modify a query
description: A saved query's criteria or columns are changed.

name: Modify an annotation
description: An annotation's name, description or values are changed.

name: Modify an annotation rule
description: An existing annotation rule's query, annotation or value is changed.

name: Modify an application
description: An application's priority, business entity or other settings are changed.

name: Modify data source settings
description: The settings of one or more data sources of the same vendor and model are changed.

name: Observe an object's performance over time
description: A dashboard with a variable and line chart widgets shows how a chosen object's metrics change over time.

name: Plan custom annotations
description: The annotation types and values needed to associate business terminology with environment data are identified.

name: Plan the business entities hierarchy
description: The levels and names of the tenant, line of business, business unit and project hierarchy are designed.

name: Run an automatic device resolution update
description: Automatic device resolution rules are re-evaluated against unidentified devices.

name: Schedule a report's output format and delivery
description: A report is scheduled with a chosen output format and delivery method such as email or saving.

name: Search for assets
description: An asset is located by name and its asset page opened.

name: Set annotation rule precedence
description: The order in which annotation rules are evaluated is changed.

name: Troubleshoot slow host performance
description: The cause of slow performance on a host is identified from its asset page performance charts and correlated resources.

name: View an asset summary
description: The summary information and metrics of an asset are displayed.

name: View asset performance charts in the Expert View
description: Performance charts for selected metrics of an asset and its related resources are displayed.

name: View asset topology
description: The topology of an asset and its connections to related assets is displayed.

name: View Insight system health
description: The current status of Insight components is displayed to identify problems.

name: View performance policy violations
description: Violations generated by performance policy thresholds are displayed and examined.

name: View predefined reports
description: The user opens the Insight Reporting portal, browses to a content folder category (for example Cloud Cost) and views the predefined Insight reports in it.

name: View queries
description: The list of saved queries is displayed and sorted or filtered.

name: View related assets of an asset
description: The assets related to a base asset are listed, filtered and optionally exported to CSV.

name: View the Assets Dashboard
description: Summary charts of the environment's assets, capacity and top utilized resources are examined to spot potential problems.

name: Locate the IBM Cognos documentation
description: Finds the IBM Cognos documentation that is installed with Insight.

name: Add a Reporting user
description: A new Data Warehouse and Reporting user account is created with a role and credentials.

name: Assign users to business entities
description: Reporting users are assigned to business entities in Cognos Administration so that multi-tenant reporting limits the data each user sees.

name: Change a user password
description: The password of an Insight user account is changed.

name: Change internal user passwords on the Data Warehouse
description: The Data Warehouse connections are updated with new passwords for the Insight internal users (dwh, inventory, dwh_internal).

name: Configure Cognos for Smart Card and certificate login
description: Cognos reporting accepts Smart Card (CAC) and certificate-based login, or CAC mode is disabled.

name: Configure Data Warehouse for Smart Card and certificate login
description: The Data Warehouse accepts Smart Card (CAC) and certificate-based login.

name: Configure LDAP for Reporting
description: LDAP authentication and authorization are enabled for Data Warehouse and Reporting users.

name: Configure LDAP user authentication
description: Insight authenticates and authorizes users through an LDAP or Active Directory server.

name: Configure the Insight server for Smart Card and certificate login
description: The Insight server accepts Smart Card (CAC) and certificate-based client authentication.

name: Create a user account
description: A new Insight user account with a role and permissions is defined.

name: Delete a user account
description: An Insight user account is removed.

name: Import CA-signed SSL certificates for Cognos and Data Warehouse
description: Cognos reporting and the Data Warehouse use CA-signed SSL certificates.

name: Modify a user account
description: An existing Insight user definition (email, role, permissions) is updated.

name: Modify Data Warehouse and Reporting user accounts
description: Edit, change the password of, activate, deactivate or delete existing Data Warehouse and Reporting user accounts.

name: Replace the Insight server SSL certificate
description: Replace the default 'ssl certificate' in the Insight server keystore (server.keystore) with a newly generated self-signed or CA-signed certificate using keytool.

name: Set a login warning message
description: A warning banner is displayed at login to the Insight server, Data Warehouse and reporting.

name: View the audit log of system and user activities
description: Audit entries of system and user activities are displayed for a chosen time period.

name: Download Insight installation packages
description: The Insight installation or upgrade packages are downloaded from the NetApp Support site or through Check for updates.

name: Install a remote acquisition unit
description: The remote acquisition unit software is installed on a server and registered with the Insight server.

name: Install Data Warehouse
description: The Data Warehouse software (with Reporting where supported) is installed on its server.

name: Install the Insight server
description: The Insight server software is installed on a server.

name: Uninstall MariaDB
description: Existing MariaDB components are removed from the Linux server before Insight is installed.

name: Verify Insight services after installation
description: Confirms that the expected Insight services are installed and running on the server after installation.

name: Verify the Data Warehouse and Reporting installation
description: Confirms that all Data Warehouse and Reporting services are present after installation.

name: Verify the remote acquisition unit installation
description: Confirms that the new remote acquisition unit service is running and that the unit is registered and connected in the Insight Acquisition Units list.

name: Add a missing disk model
description: A disk model not recognized by data sources is added to the new disk models file.

name: Calculate the number of database objects
description: The calculated scale report shows the number of objects in the Insight database.

name: Check the status of server resources
description: The status of Insight server resources is displayed.

name: Collect logs for NetApp Support
description: Insight server, acquisition or remote logs are generated or bundled into a file for NetApp Support.

name: Configure ASUP
description: AutoSupport processing is enabled and configured for sending Insight data to NetApp.

name: Configure the number of hours to ignore dynamic data
description: Insight ignores dynamic attribute changes for the specified number of hours.

name: Disable automatic ASUP transmissions
description: Data Warehouse stops sending its daily AutoSupport report.

name: Find ghost data sources
description: Data sources that report devices already reported by other data sources are listed.

name: Include a Data Warehouse database backup in ASUP
description: ASUP transmissions are configured to include a backup of the Data Warehouse database.

name: Resolve annotation consolidation issues
description: Conflicting annotations for an object that several Insight servers report are identified and resolved in Data Warehouse.

name: Scrub support data before transfer to NetApp Support
description: Sensitive keywords are scrubbed from data sent to NetApp Support.

name: Send diagnostic data to NetApp Support
description: Logs, recordings and performance data are sent to NetApp Support on demand.

name: Send Insight logs to ASUP
description: An Insight log bundle is downloaded from the Data Warehouse Troubleshooting page and sent to NetApp through ASUP.

name: Submit an online technical support request
description: A support case is opened on the NetApp Support site with a package of troubleshooting data attached.

name: Troubleshoot a failed data source
description: The cause of a failed or slow data source is identified from its summary, event history and patch information.

name: Troubleshoot an application performance problem
description: An application's performance problem is investigated from its landing page through its related compute and storage resources to find the cause.

name: View chassis consolidation issues
description: Displays hosts and adapters, storage arrays or switches reported by several Insight servers that Data Warehouse has to consolidate.

name: View Insight logs
description: Insight log files are opened from the Data Warehouse Troubleshooting page.

name: View installed Insight components
description: The installed Insight software packages and versions are listed.

name: View system information
description: System information about the Insight server is displayed.

name: Apply an Insight service pack
description: An Insight service pack with fixes and enhancements is applied.

name: Commit a data source patch
description: A data source patch under review is made permanent after verifying it works as expected.

name: Install a data source patch
description: Apply a data source patch to update or add data source types.

name: Migrate Insight from Windows to Linux
description: An Insight installation is moved from a Windows server to a Linux server by backing up, installing on Linux and restoring the database.

name: Restore Reporting artifacts from an earlier release
description: Reporting artifacts exported from an Insight release earlier than 6.3 are imported into the current Reporting server using Insight Reporting Administration.

name: Roll back a data source patch
description: A data source patch that does not perform as expected is removed and the previous version restored.

name: Uninstall a remote acquisition unit
description: The remote acquisition unit software is removed from its server.

name: Uninstall Data Warehouse
description: The Data Warehouse software is removed from its server.

name: Uninstall the Insight server
description: The Insight server software is removed from its server.

name: Update disk models
description: The diskmodels.jar file on the Insight server is replaced with a newer version so that new disk models are recognized.

name: Upgrade a remote acquisition unit
description: The remote acquisition unit software is upgraded to a newer release.

name: Upgrade Data Warehouse
description: The Data Warehouse software is upgraded to a newer release, with the database, reports and vault backed up and restored.

name: Upgrade the Insight server
description: The Insight server software is upgraded to a newer release.

name: Verify that Data Warehouse has historical data
description: A custom report is run to confirm that Data Warehouse still has its historical data after an upgrade.

name: View data source patch status
description: The status of data source patches under review is displayed.

name: Add a data source
description: A data source (such as a Unified Manager server) is added to WFA so that it can acquire data from it.

name: Add a remote system type
description: A new remote system type is defined in WFA so it can connect to additional kinds of systems.

name: Add approval points to a workflow
description: Approval points are inserted into a workflow so that execution pauses until a user approves it.

name: Add entities to a workflow pack
description: Workflows, commands, finders or other entities are added to a WFA workflow pack.

name: Check in a workflow pack to the SCM repository
description: A workflow pack is exported to a server folder under source control management so it is versioned in the SCM repository.

name: Configure a database user for data acquisition
description: A read-only database user is created on the monitoring server so WFA can acquire data from its database.

name: Configure protocols for connecting to remote systems
description: The connection protocol and port that WFA uses to reach a remote system type are set.

name: Configure resource reservation for workflows
description: Command resource reservation is enabled and its expiration period is set for workflows.

name: Create a cache query
description: A SQL cache query is created that populates a dictionary entry from a data source type.

name: Create a command
description: A new WFA command definition with properties, code and parameters is created for use in workflows.

name: Create a data source type
description: A new data source type with its acquisition method and default port is defined in WFA.

name: Create a dictionary entry
description: A new dictionary entry describing an object type and its attributes is created in a WFA scheme.

name: Create a filter
description: A new filter with a SQL query is created for use by finders and workflows.

name: Create a finder
description: A new finder combining one or more filters is created to locate resources in workflows.

name: Create a function
description: A new reusable function is created and tested for use in workflow expressions.

name: Create a recurring schedule
description: A recurring schedule is created so that workflows can be run at a set frequency.

name: Create a scheme
description: A new data scheme is created in WFA.

name: Create a template
description: A new template holding attribute values for a dictionary object is created for use in commands.

name: Create a workflow
description: A new workflow is built from commands, user inputs, approval points and other building blocks.

name: Create a workflow pack
description: A new WFA workflow pack with a name, author, version and description is created.

name: Create workflow help content
description: HTML help content is authored, packaged as a zip file and attached to a workflow.

name: Customize a predefined workflow
description: A predefined workflow is cloned and the copy is edited to meet specific requirements.

name: Define filter rules for a workflow
description: Rules are defined in a workflow to filter the resources that the workflow selects.

name: Delete a scheme
description: An existing WFA scheme is removed.

name: Delete workflow packs
description: A workflow pack is removed from WFA.

name: Disable cache acquisition for a dictionary entry
description: Data acquisition into the WFA cache is disabled for a selected dictionary entry.

name: Export Workflow Automation content
description: User-created WFA content such as workflows, commands and finders is exported to a .dar file for sharing.

name: Import Workflow Automation content
description: WFA content from a .dar file is imported into WFA.

name: Import workflow packs from the server
description: A workflow pack from a server or SCM folder is imported into WFA, adding it or updating an existing pack.

name: Modify a scheme
description: The properties of an existing WFA scheme are changed.

name: Remove entities from a workflow pack
description: Entities are removed from a workflow pack and the updated pack can be checked in to SCM.

name: Roll back a workflow pack to a previous version from SCM
description: A workflow pack is rolled back to an earlier version in the source control repository and re-imported into WFA.

name: Test the reservation script for a command
description: A command's reservation script is checked against a copy of the WFA database in the playground database.

name: Back up and restore the database and configurations in a high-availability setup
description: The WFA database and supported configurations of a high-availability deployment are backed up and restored for disaster recovery.

name: Configure an earlier version of Workflow Automation for high availability
description: An existing earlier WFA installation is upgraded, backed up and reinstalled across cluster nodes so it runs in a high-availability configuration.

name: Configure Workflow Automation for high availability in a cluster
description: WFA data is moved to shared storage and WFA services are configured as cluster resources on both nodes.

name: Prepare a failover cluster for Workflow Automation installation
description: The cluster software and shared LUNs are configured on both nodes so WFA can be installed for high availability.

name: Uninstall Workflow Automation from a high-availability cluster
description: WFA is removed from both cluster nodes, and its cluster resources and shared data are deleted.

name: Configure the preferred Perl distribution
description: WFA is configured to use a chosen Perl distribution instead of the default one.

name: Configure the web GUI timeout value
description: The WFA web GUI timeout is changed from its default of 180 seconds.

name: Install site-specific Perl modules
description: Site-specific Perl modules are installed with PPM into a user module area outside the WFA installation directory, so a WFA upgrade does not delete them.

name: Modify the database transaction timeout
description: The WFA database transaction timeout is increased from its default of 300 seconds, for example before restoring a large database.

name: Back up the WFA database
description: A full or regular backup of the WFA database (and optionally its configurations) is created for later recovery.

name: Restore the WFA database
description: A previously created full or regular backup of the WFA database is restored.

name: Configure email notifications
description: Mail server settings are configured so WFA sends email notifications about workflow operations.

name: Configure email notifications for data source acquisition failures
description: The threshold and interval at which WFA emails about data source acquisition failures are configured.

name: Configure SNMP
description: WFA is configured to send SNMP traps about workflow operation status to a management host.

name: Configure Syslog
description: WFA is configured to send log events to a Syslog server at a chosen log level.

name: Add Active Directory groups
description: Active Directory groups are added to WFA and mapped to WFA roles.

name: Configure authentication settings
description: WFA is configured to authenticate users against Active Directory or LDAP servers.

name: Configure the credentials of a target system
description: Credentials are stored in WFA for a target storage or remote system so workflows can connect to it.

name: Create a certificate signing request
description: A certificate signing request is generated for the WFA server so a CA-signed SSL certificate can be obtained.

name: Create local users
description: New local WFA users with assigned roles are created.

name: Disable the default password policy
description: The password policy that WFA enforces for local users is disabled.

name: Enable remote access to the Workflow Automation database
description: The WFA database is made reachable by clients on other hosts (or restricted back to local-only access).

name: Modify the default password policy
description: The password policy that WFA enforces for local users is changed to custom requirements.

name: Replace the default SSL certificate
description: The default self-signed WFA SSL certificate is replaced with a new or CA-signed certificate.

name: Reset the admin password created during installation
description: The password of the WFA admin user created during installation is reset from the WFA server shell.

name: Restrict the access rights of Workflow Automation on the host
description: The WFA services run under a dedicated, less-privileged host user account instead of the host administrator.

name: Access Workflow Automation
description: The user signs in to the WFA web GUI as admin and completes initial setup of credentials and a data source.

name: Install OnCommand Workflow Automation
description: WFA is installed on a Linux or Windows server, for example on a cluster node.

name: Install required Perl modules
description: The Perl modules WFA requires are verified and installed from the configured repositories on the Linux host.

name: Configure AutoSupport
description: AutoSupport is enabled and configured so WFA sends AutoSupport messages to technical support.

name: Repair the ActivePerl installation
description: A broken ActivePerl installation used by WFA is repaired by backing up the database, reinstalling WFA and restoring the database.

name: Troubleshoot a blank Workflow Automation web page
description: A WFA web GUI that shows a blank page on Windows Server is fixed by installing the required Windows Desktop Experience/Flash features.

name: Migrate the Workflow Automation installation
description: A WFA installation, including its database and key, is moved to a different host.

name: Uninstall OnCommand Workflow Automation
description: WFA is removed from a standalone Windows or Linux host.

name: Upgrade ActiveState Perl
description: The ActiveState Perl distribution on the WFA host is upgraded to a newer supported version.

name: Upgrade MySQL
description: The MySQL server used by WFA is upgraded to a newer supported version.

name: Upgrade OnCommand Workflow Automation
description: An existing WFA installation is upgraded to a newer WFA release.

name: Upgrade OpenJDK
description: The OpenJDK runtime used by WFA is upgraded to a newer version.

name: Manage storage systems in the CIMOM repository
description: Adds, deletes, or lists storage systems in the CIMOM repository, and lists their NFS and CIFS exports and exported LUNs.

name: Set the automatic cache refresh interval
description: Sets how often SMI-S Provider refreshes its cache automatically through the CACHE_REFRESH_SEC environment variable and restarts the CIM server.

name: Set the concrete job lifetime
description: Sets how long SMI-S Provider keeps concrete jobs through the JOB_LIFETIME_SEC environment variable.

name: Set the maximum number of threads per message service queue
description: Sets the maximum number of threads per message service queue through the PEGASUS_MAX_THREADS_PER_SVC_QUEUE environment variable and restarts the CIM server.

name: Set the ONTAP API call timeout
description: Sets the ONTAP API call timeout used by SMI-S Provider through the ONTAPI_TIMEOUT_SEC environment variable.

name: Start, stop, or restart the CIM server
description: The CIM server service of SMI-S Provider is started, stopped, or restarted as needed.

name: Configure log settings
description: Sets the logging level and log location for SMI-S Provider system messages and restarts the CIM server.

name: Enable indications
description: Turns on SMI-S Provider indications by setting PEGASUS_DISABLE_INDICATIONS to false and restarting the CIM server.

name: Configure CIMOM HTTP and HTTPS connection settings
description: Enables or disables HTTP and HTTPS connections to the CIMOM, changes their port numbers, and restarts the CIM server.

name: Add a CIM server user
description: Creates a local administrator account and registers it as a CIM user that is allowed to use the CIM server.

name: Enable or disable audit logging of SMI-S commands
description: Turns audit logging of incoming SMI-S commands on or off at runtime.

name: Enable or disable SMI-S Provider authentication
description: Turns authentication for SMI-S Provider on or off and restarts the provider.

name: Generate a self-signed certificate for the CIM server
description: Uses OpenSSL to generate a self-signed certificate for the CIM server, then restarts the CIM server so it uses the certificate.

name: Manage CIM server users
description: Adds, removes, or lists the CIM users authorized to use the CIM server, or changes their passwords.

name: Download the SMI-S Provider software package
description: Downloads the SMI-S Provider installation package from the NetApp Support Site before deployment.

name: Install SMI-S Provider
description: Installs SMI-S Provider on the host by running the software package's setup wizard.

name: Verify that a storage system works with SMI-S Provider
description: Adds at least one storage system to the CIMOM repository and checks the command output to confirm the system works correctly with SMI-S Provider.

name: Verify the CIM server status
description: Confirms after installation that the CIM server started automatically and is running.

name: Configure trace settings
description: Sets the SMI-S Provider trace settings used for troubleshooting and restarts the CIM server.

name: Set the number of trace files saved
description: Sets how many trace files are kept through the PEGASUS_TRACE_FILE_NUM environment variable and restarts the CIM server.

name: Set the trace file size
description: Sets the maximum trace file size through the PEGASUS_TRACE_FILE_SIZE environment variable and restarts the CIM server.

name: Uninstall SMI-S Provider
description: Removes SMI-S Provider from the host through the operating system's program removal tool.

name: Discover new mailboxes, sites, and groups
description: Synchronizes a service with Microsoft 365 so that newly added users, sites and groups appear in SaaS Backup.

name: Activate a service
description: Activates a Microsoft 365 service, such as Exchange, OneDrive or SharePoint, so that SaaS Backup can protect it.

name: Apply existing rules
description: Runs an existing rule against unprotected items so that matching items are moved to its backup tier.

name: Browse backups
description: Browses the backed-up items of an account, such as mail, calendar, tasks, contacts or files, for a selected time range.

name: Cancel a job
description: Stops a running backup or restore job, which then appears under recent completed jobs.

name: Create a rule
description: Creates a filter-based rule that assigns matching unprotected items to a backup policy tier automatically.

name: Deactivate a service
description: Deactivates a Microsoft 365 service so that SaaS Backup stops protecting it.

name: Delete a rule
description: Removes an existing rule for assigning items to backup policy tiers.

name: Enable Advanced Search for users
description: Turns on Advanced Search for selected Exchange Online users so that their backed-up data is indexed for searching.

name: Enable OneNote backups
description: Turns on backup of OneNote notebooks in the Microsoft 365 backup settings.

name: Migrate backup data
description: Moves backup data to a different storage target after the storage connection is entered and tested in the Data Migration settings.

name: Modify backup settings
description: Changes the service-specific backup options in the Microsoft 365 backup settings.

name: Modify the backup retention period
description: Changes how long backup data is kept, either for individual users and tenants or for a backup policy tier.

name: Perform a granular-level restore for Exchange Online
description: Restores an entire Exchange mailbox category or specific items in a category from backup.

name: Perform a granular-level restore for Microsoft 365 Groups and Teams
description: Restores selected channels, mailbox items or SharePoint site content of a Microsoft 365 group or team from backup.

name: Perform a granular-level restore for OneDrive for Business
description: Restores selected files from a backed-up OneDrive for Business MySite.

name: Perform a granular-level restore for SharePoint Online
description: Restores a selected category of a SharePoint Online site from the most recent or an earlier backup.

name: Perform a high-level service restore
description: Restores a whole mailbox, group, team, MySite or site of a service using the selected restore option.

name: Perform an immediate backup
description: Starts an on-demand backup job outside the schedule for selected service items or for all items in a backup policy tier.

name: Purge the backup data of a user, site collection, or Microsoft 365 group
description: Permanently deletes the backup data of a selected user, site collection or Microsoft 365 group for a service.

name: Restore from a previous backup
description: Restores an item from a chosen earlier backup in its backup history.

name: Schedule a backup
description: Moves mailboxes, sites or groups into a backup policy tier so that they are protected and backed up at that tier's frequency, or changes their tier to change the backup frequency.

name: Search backed-up items
description: Search protected instances by name, or run an Advanced Search of backed-up Exchange Online items, to find content to review or restore.

name: View deleted items
description: Turns on the Show Deleted Items setting and displays items that were deleted in Microsoft 365.

name: View deprovisioned items
description: Lists the items of a service that were deprovisioned in Microsoft 365.

name: View previous Advanced Search jobs
description: Finds a previously run Advanced Search job and displays its results.

name: View purged data
description: Displays the list of users, sites and groups whose backup data has been purged.

name: Add a license
description: Adds and validates a new subscription license for SaaS Backup.

name: Release a user license
description: Frees the license assigned to a user account so that another user can use it.

name: Update subscription information
description: Updates the subscription details of the SaaS Backup account by signing in with the original sign-up credentials.

name: Configure notifications
description: Adds email addresses to the accounts that receive SaaS Backup notifications.

name: Create a user-defined filter
description: Filters a service's list of protected or unprotected items by selected criteria.

name: Download a completed job log
description: Download the log of a completed backup or restore job, which for restore jobs lists the names and locations of the restored files.

name: Download the activity log
description: Downloads the list of all SaaS Backup activity from the Reporting Activity Log tab to a local file.

name: Export user data
description: Exports an Excel file of the user data for a service so that it can be monitored.

name: View job history
description: Displays, and optionally filters by policy, service or other criteria, the history of SaaS Backup jobs.

name: View the activity log
description: Displays, and optionally filters by service or event, the list of all SaaS Backup activity.

name: Submit feedback
description: Completes and submits the in-product feedback survey.

name: Add a security group
description: Adds a Microsoft 365 security group to SaaS Backup account settings.

name: Assign administrative roles to a user account
description: Grants SaaS Backup administrative roles to a user account in Role Management.

name: Configure impersonation for Exchange Online
description: Manually assigns the ApplicationImpersonation admin role to the service account in Exchange Online so that SaaS Backup can access mailboxes.

name: Create a service account
description: Create a Microsoft 365 service account with the required administrator permissions and add it to SaaS Backup, as the primary account or as an additional account so more backups can run at once.

name: Delete a security group
description: Removes a security group from SaaS Backup account settings.

name: Enable Modern Authentication
description: Turns on Modern Authentication for the tenant by confirming the prompt and accepting the requested permissions.

name: Grant permissions to enable shared mailboxes
description: Grants tenant consent so that SaaS Backup can discover and back up shared mailboxes.

name: Modify administrative roles of a user account
description: Changes the SaaS Backup administrative roles assigned to an existing user account in Role Management.

name: Remove all administrative roles from a user account
description: Deletes a user from Role Management, removing all of the SaaS Backup administrative roles assigned to that user.

name: Synchronize user permissions with Azure Active Directory

description: Download the Disaster Recovery Orchestrator package to a designated VM, run its deployment script and access its UI.

name: Create an FSx for ONTAP volume
description: Create a volume on an FSx for ONTAP SVM from the AWS console with the required size and snapshot-only tiering policy.

name: Set up managed OpenShift on AWS with FSx for ONTAP storage
description: Provisions an FSx for ONTAP file system in the ROSA cluster VPC, installs Trident, creates backends and storage classes, and deploys a stateful test application.

name: Add a managed cluster to Advanced Cluster Management
description: Brings an OpenShift cluster under Advanced Cluster Management either by creating a new cluster through a provider connection or by importing an existing cluster with the generated agent command.

name: Learn about Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes
description: Describes the multi-cluster lifecycle, application, observability and governance capabilities of Advanced Cluster Management with NetApp storage.

name: Back up and restore container applications with NetApp Backup and Recovery
description: Discovers a Kubernetes cluster in NetApp Console, configures ONTAP or ONTAP S3 as the backup target, backs up container applications and restores them.

name: Learn about data protection for containers and VMs with third-party tools
description: Links to procedures for backing up and restoring container applications and OpenShift Virtualization VMs with third-party tools.

name: Learn about data protection for containers and VMs with Trident Protect
description: Links to procedures for creating snapshots and backups and restoring container applications and OpenShift Virtualization VMs with Trident Protect.

name: Configure NFS client slot table entries on worker nodes
description: Uses a MachineConfig to set the maximum sunrpc slot table entries on worker nodes to 128 to match ONTAP NFS concurrency and reboots the nodes to apply it.

name: Create a private image registry with persistent storage
description: Configures the OpenShift image registry operator to use Trident-provisioned persistent storage and exposes the registry through a route.

name: Deploy an application from the cloud console marketplace
description: Deploys an application such as WordPress with Trident-provisioned persistent storage to a Kubernetes cluster from the Google Cloud Console Marketplace.

name: Deploy Jenkins with persistent storage
description: Creates a Jenkins project and its required resources and instantiates the Jenkins persistent template so Jenkins runs with Trident-provisioned persistent storage.

name: Learn about NetApp storage for vSphere Kubernetes Service
description: Describes the benefits of NetApp storage for VKS, the supported ONTAP platforms and protocols, and how the Trident NAS and SAN drivers map PVCs to ONTAP volumes, qtrees and LUNs.

name: Learn about vSphere Kubernetes Service
description: Describes the key features and use cases of VMware vSphere Kubernetes Service.

name: Expose an application service through a load balancer
description: Changes an application's service type from ClusterIP to LoadBalancer so the application gets an external IP address.

name: Install the F5 BIG-IP load balancer
description: Installs the F5 AS3 extension and the BIG-IP container ingress services and IPAM controller in the Kubernetes cluster, then verifies that LoadBalancer services receive external IPs.

name: Install the MetalLB load balancer
description: Deploys MetalLB into the cluster and configures it so services of type LoadBalancer receive external IP addresses.

name: Add a tenant project to a multi-tenant cluster
description: Adds a new isolated project to a multi-tenant OpenShift cluster by creating a dedicated SVM, Trident backend, storage class, resource quotas and developer role for it.

name: Create a governance compliance policy
description: Creates a governance and risk compliance policy in Advanced Cluster Management and applies it to managed clusters to monitor and enforce compliance.

name: Create tenant projects and developer roles
description: As cluster administrator, creates the tenant projects and the per-project developer roles and group bindings that restrict users to their own project.

name: Review multi-tenancy technology requirements
description: Lists the components (ONTAP cluster, OpenShift cluster, Trident) required for the multi-tenancy architecture.

name: Verify multi-tenant project access isolation
description: Confirms that a project developer can create PVCs and pods only in the assigned project with its dedicated storage class and cannot view or edit projects, resource quotas or storage classes belonging to other tenants.

name: Deploy a vSphere Kubernetes Service cluster
description: Creates a VKS cluster, downloads its kubeconfig from vCenter and connects to it from a bastion host for management.

name: Deploy Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes
description: Installs the Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes operator on a hub OpenShift cluster and creates the MultiClusterHub so multiple clusters can be managed centrally.

name: Install an OpenShift cluster using installer-provisioned infrastructure
description: Deploys a Red Hat OpenShift cluster with the installer-provisioned infrastructure method by downloading the installer, pull secret and CLI tools and running the installation.

name: Configure a Trident backend and storage class
description: Create Trident storage backends (for example ONTAP NFS or Element iSCSI) and the matching Kubernetes storage classes (and a snapshot class), then apply them to the cluster.

name: Configure dedicated storage for tenant projects
description: As storage administrator, creates a dedicated SVM, Trident backend, storage class and storage resource quotas for each tenant project so that each project consumes only its own storage.

name: Set the default Trident storage class and snapshot class
description: Marks a Trident StorageClass and VolumeSnapshotClass as the cluster defaults so PVCs and snapshots without an explicit class use Trident.

name: Configure AWX/Tower inventory, hosts, and credentials
description: The AWX/Tower inventory, groups, hosts, credential types and ONTAP and Oracle credentials needed by the database automation are created.

name: Connect a Windows host to iSCSI volumes
description: The Windows SQL Server node connects to the iSCSI targets of its volumes so the disks can be brought online and used.

name: Create a host group
description: A host group containing the iSCSI initiator names collected from the SQL nodes is created so the nodes can access the iSCSI volumes.

name: Provision iSCSI storage for an Oracle database
description: iSCSI storage pools, host groups and volumes are created and the database hosts are connected over iSCSI with multipath for Oracle ASM.

name: Configure cluster quorum settings
description: The failover cluster quorum is set to use a file share witness.

name: Configure Oracle Data Guard Broker and Fast-Start Failover
description: Data Guard Broker is enabled and Fast-Start Failover is configured with an observer so the standby takes over automatically.

name: Configure possible owners for the availability group listener resource
description: The distributed network name resource is limited to the nodes that take part in the availability group.

name: Create a file share for a cluster witness
description: A Windows shared folder is created on the witness server for use as the cluster file share witness.

name: Create a Windows Server failover cluster
description: A failover cluster is created from the SQL Server nodes after its validation tests pass.

name: Create an Oracle standby database using storage replication seeding
description: An Oracle Data Guard standby database is created by seeding its storage through volume replication and registering it with Oracle Restart.

name: Enable Always On availability groups on SQL Server
description: The Always On High Availability feature is enabled on the SQL Server service so that availability groups can be created.

name: Fail over an Oracle database to a SnapMirror standby
description: SnapMirror replication is broken, the replicated volumes are mounted on the standby host, the Oracle database is recovered there, and replication can later be resynchronized.

name: Finalize an Oracle Data Guard standby database
description: Standby redo logs, flashback, managed recovery and redo shipping are enabled, and the Data Guard state is verified.

name: Install required Windows features for failover clustering
description: The Failover Clustering and Multipath I/O features are installed on the SQL Server nodes.

name: Validate and configure a disaster recovery clone database
description: A database cloned at the DR site is confirmed to include the last replicated transactions, is configured for use, and its clone volume is split from the replica.

name: Migrate a SQL Server database to the cloud
description: An on-premises SQL Server database is backed up, copied to cloud file storage and restored on a cloud SQL Server VM.

name: Migrate an Oracle database from on-premises to the cloud
description: Move an on-premises Oracle database to a cloud database host and storage using SnapMirror replication, a backup copy staged through object storage, or PDB relocation.

name: Provision a cloud compute instance for a database server
description: A correctly sized cloud virtual machine is launched and prepared to host an Oracle or SQL Server database.

name: Review public cloud prerequisites for hybrid cloud database solutions
description: Lists the logins, network access, connector location and cloud permissions needed before running hybrid cloud database workloads.

name: Add a transaction log backup policy to a resource group
description: An existing SnapCenter resource group is modified to include a scheduled transaction log backup policy for its databases.

name: Archive database Snapshot copies to cloud object storage
description: Database Snapshot copies are transferred for long-term retention to cloud blob storage with AzCopy.

name: Configure automated Oracle data protection
description: AWX/Tower job templates are created, launched and scheduled to set up and schedule replication of Oracle binary, data and log volumes.

name: Configure AzAcSnap for Oracle database snapshots
description: AzAcSnap is set up to take application-consistent Oracle snapshots by creating the database user, Oracle wallet, Azure service principal connectivity and the azacsnap configuration file, then testing it.

name: Configure scheduled backup protection for databases
description: One or more databases are protected in SnapCenter by a resource group or protection wizard that applies backup policies, schedules, verification and notifications.

name: Install AzAcSnap
description: The Azure Application Consistent Snapshot tool is downloaded and installed on the database host.

name: Run an on-demand database backup
description: An immediate Snapshot-based full or log backup of a database or resource group is taken with SnapCenter Backup Now.

name: Set up SnapCenter for database backup and recovery
description: SnapCenter is prepared to protect SQL Server databases by configuring credentials, storage connections, host plug-ins and backup policies.

name: Set up SnapMirror replication for database volumes
description: Cluster and SVM peering are established and SnapMirror relationships replicate database volumes from the primary to the secondary or cloud cluster.

name: Add a database host and install the SnapCenter plug-in
description: A Linux or Windows database host is added to SnapCenter with credentials, and the database plug-in is installed on it.

name: Add a storage SVM to SnapCenter
description: A database storage SVM (for example on Cloud Volumes ONTAP) is registered as a storage system in SnapCenter.

name: Configure a cloned database for dev/test use
description: A newly cloned Oracle or SQL Server database is adjusted for dev/test use by changing its log mode and configuring the listener.

name: Configure a cloud instance as a standby database host
description: A cloud instance is set up with DNS, credentials, domain membership, storage and a database installation that matches on-premises, so it can act as a SnapCenter-managed standby host.

name: Configure SnapCenter credentials for plug-in installation
description: The Windows or SQL authentication credentials that SnapCenter needs to install plug-ins and discover instances are set up and assigned.

name: Configure SQL Server for an availability group
description: The SQL Server services are set to run under domain service accounts with the required logins, and the system databases are moved to new storage paths.

name: Convert a non-CDB Oracle database to a PDB
description: A single-instance non-CDB Oracle database is plugged into a multitenant container database as a PDB.

name: Create a database on a SQL Server instance
description: A new user database is created on the first SQL Server instance so it can be added to an availability group.

name: Create an Oracle database on an existing Oracle host
description: A new Oracle database (CDB/PDB) is created on a host where the Oracle software is already installed, either with DBCA on ASM disk groups (registered with Oracle Restart) or by rerunning the NetApp Ansible automation with only the oracle_config tag.

name: Deploy an Oracle database on NFS storage
description: Oracle is installed and a database is created on ONTAP NFS storage by running the NetApp Ansible automation toolkit after downloading the repo and filling in the inventory and variables.

name: Deploy PostgreSQL with high availability and disaster recovery
description: A PostgreSQL primary/standby deployment with disaster recovery is provisioned on cloud compute and FSx for ONTAP using the automation toolkit.

name: Install Oracle Grid Infrastructure and Database software
description: Oracle Grid Infrastructure and the Oracle Database software are installed on each database host.

name: Join database servers to an Active Directory domain
description: The SQL Server VMs are joined to the Active Directory domain.

name: Review Oracle deployment tasks by high availability tier
description: Lists linked deployment tasks for each Oracle high availability tier.

name: Verify an Oracle database installation
description: The deployed Oracle instance, database configuration, PDBs and listener are checked to confirm the installation succeeded.

name: Configure firewall rules for SQL Server cluster nodes
description: The required ports for SQL Server and cluster communication are opened on both SQL nodes.

name: Add a database administrator user to SnapCenter
description: A database management user from Active Directory is added to SnapCenter and assigned the appropriate role.

name: Create a storage pool
description: A cloud NetApp storage pool is created with the required capacity and performance.

name: Provision NFS database volumes for Oracle
description: NFS volumes for Oracle binaries, data and logs are created in the cloud NetApp storage account with suitable naming and protocol settings.

name: Acquire AWS access and secret keys for Cloud Volumes ONTAP deployment
description: An AWS access key and secret key are generated and kept for automated deployment of the Connector and Cloud Volumes ONTAP.

name: Acquire the NetApp Cloud API client ID
description: The client ID for NetApp Cloud API authentication is copied from the developer hub for use in automated Connector and Cloud Volumes ONTAP deployment.

name: Generate a NetApp Cloud Central refresh token
description: A refresh token is generated from NetApp Cloud Central and saved for automated Connector and Cloud Volumes ONTAP deployment.

name: Review prerequisites for Cloud Volumes automation with Terraform
description: Lists what Terraform-based Cloud Volumes automation needs: Terraform version, a Cloud Manager account, a cloud provider account and a host machine.

name: Analyze file data with XCP file analytics
description: XCP scans list files by age and report the space and total size used by data not modified within a set period.

name: Create an ONTAP cyber vault
description: A destination cluster becomes an air-gapped cyber vault: the SnapLock compliance clock is initialized, SnapLock Compliance data protection volumes are created, and SnapVault relationships are set up and initialized.

name: Harden an ONTAP cyber vault
description: The cyber vault cluster is hardened with multi-admin verification, encryption of in-flight data, secure SSH, FIPS mode, dedicated admin roles, an isolated IPspace and SVM, disabled unused protocols and tightened firewall policies.

name: Size an ONTAP cyber vault for performance
description: Lists the questions for sizing a cyber vault, such as source platforms, bandwidth and latency, file counts and sizes, and recovery time objectives.

name: Troubleshoot an XCP 'no space left on device' error
description: An XCP nfs3 error 28 on a destination volume that still has free space is fixed by checking inode usage and raising the volume's inode count.

name: Migrate HDFS or MapR-FS data to NFS with XCP
description: Data in an HDFS or MapR-FS data lake is migrated by a non-root user to a NetApp NFS volume with XCP.

name: Migrate NFS data to ONTAP with XCP
description: NFS file data from a 7-Mode system or a third-party NAS is copied to an ONTAP NFS volume with XCP (scan, baseline copy, incremental sync, verify). XCP setup and subdirectory-level migration are optional parts of the same procedure.

name: Migrate SMB data to ONTAP with XCP
description: SMB/CIFS file data, with or without ACLs, is copied from a source storage system to an ONTAP SMB share with XCP, then synced and verified.

name: Migrate volume Snapshot copies from 7-Mode to ONTAP with XCP
description: Snapshot copies of a 7-Mode source volume are moved to an ONTAP destination volume using XCP baseline copy and incremental sync.

name: Create and map LUNs for SAP HANA
description: The volumes and LUNs needed for SAP HANA data, log and shared file systems are created and mapped to an initiator group for the HANA hosts.

name: Configure SnapMirror active sync replication for SAP HANA
description: Consistency groups for the SAP HANA storage units are created and protected with SnapMirror active sync in active/active mode.

name: Create volumes from Snapshot backups at the disaster recovery site
description: New volumes with file path and export policy are created from application-consistent Snapshot backups at the disaster recovery site.

name: Fail over SAP HANA to the disaster recovery site
description: Replication is broken, the data volume restored to the latest application-consistent snapshot, volumes mounted at the target host and SAP HANA recovered at the disaster recovery site.

name: Test SAP HANA disaster recovery
description: New volumes are created from replicated snapshot backups at the disaster recovery site, mounted on a target host and the HANA database recovered to validate the disaster recovery workflow.

name: Add a storage system to SnapCenter
description: An ONTAP cluster or SVM is registered in SnapCenter as primary or secondary (backup) storage.

name: Configure Azure NetApp Files cross-region replication for SAP HANA
description: The disaster recovery site is prepared with a NetApp account, capacity pool and delegated subnet, and cross-region replication is set up for the SAP HANA volumes.

name: Configure protection for an SAP HANA database resource in SnapCenter
description: An auto-discovered SAP HANA database resource is configured with its user store key, Snapshot naming format, policies and schedules in SnapCenter.

name: Configure SnapCenter for SAP HANA backup
description: SnapCenter is set up for SAP HANA with backup user, credentials, storage systems, plug-in hosts, policies and resource protection.

name: Configure SnapCenter protection for an IBM Db2 database in an SAP environment
description: The Db2 host and database prerequisites are checked, the SnapCenter agent is deployed and the Db2 database of the SAP system is protected with SnapCenter.

name: Configure SnapCenter protection for an SAP ASE database
description: The ASE host and database prerequisites are checked, the SnapCenter agent is deployed and the ASE database of the SAP system is protected with SnapCenter.

name: Configure SnapCenter protection for an SAP HANA System Replication environment
description: The HANA plug-in is installed on both System Replication hosts and a resource group covering both hosts is created and protected in SnapCenter.

name: Configure SnapCenter protection for an SAP MaxDB database
description: The MaxDB host and database prerequisites are checked, the SnapCenter agent is deployed and the MaxDB database of the SAP system is protected with SnapCenter.

name: Configure SnapCenter protection for SAP HANA non-data volumes
description: A non-data volume resource with its SVM and volumes is added in SnapCenter so that non-data volumes of SAP HANA are backed up.

name: Configure SnapVault backup replication for SAP HANA
description: File systems and SVMs are peered, a DP target volume, vault policy and SnapMirror relationship are created, and SnapCenter is configured to replicate SAP HANA backups.

name: Create a SnapCenter block integrity check policy for SAP HANA
description: A file-based backup policy for SAP HANA block integrity checks with weekly frequency and retention is created in SnapCenter.

name: Create a SnapCenter Snapshot backup policy for SAP HANA
description: A Snapshot-based backup policy with schedule frequency and retention is created in SnapCenter for SAP HANA.

name: Create an on-demand SAP HANA Snapshot backup
description: An on-demand Snapshot backup of an SAP HANA resource is run from SnapCenter using a selected backup policy.

name: Disable auto discovery on the SAP HANA plug-in host
description: SnapCenter automatic discovery for SAP HANA is turned off on a plug-in host using the Set-SmConfigSettings command.

name: Manage SAP HANA log backup retention with SnapCenter
description: Describes how SnapCenter automatically deletes SAP HANA log backups older than the oldest retained data backup.

name: Protect SAP HANA on VMware VMFS with SnapCenter and SnapMirror active sync
description: Scope list of the solution covering LUN creation, ESXi host access, consistency groups, SnapMirror active sync and SnapCenter protection of SAP HANA on VMFS.

name: Protect SAP HANA with SnapCenter
description: Overview of SnapCenter SAP HANA backup capabilities including scheduling, retention, catalog housekeeping and restore.

name: Restore an SAP HANA System Replication system from a SnapCenter backup
description: Restore and recover an SAP HANA database in a System Replication environment from a SnapCenter Snapshot backup. The backup can come from the local host or from the other replication host, and the restore can use the valid backup alone or the valid backup plus a crash image.

name: Restore and recover a single SAP HANA tenant database
description: A single SAP HANA tenant database is restored with SnapCenter and recovered using SAP HANA Studio.

name: Add an SAP HANA plug-in host to SnapCenter
description: A Linux host is added to SnapCenter and the SAP HANA plug-in is deployed on it, either on the database host or on a central plug-in host.

name: Add data volume partitions to an SAP HANA system
description: Additional data volume partitions are enabled in SAP HANA and the additional LUNs or volumes are configured, formatted and mounted on the database host.

name: Clone an SAP system
description: A clone of an SAP system with the same SID is created from a Snapshot backup on a target host, including the HANA shared and data volumes and database recovery.

name: Configure Fibre Channel networking for SAP HANA on SUSE KVM
description: Physical FC HBA ports are assigned to SAP HANA KVM virtual machines as PCI devices to provide redundant FCP connections to storage.

name: Configure multipathing on an SAP HANA host
description: The HANA hosts discover the new LUNs and the multipath configuration is set with WWID aliases for the data and log LUNs.

name: Configure SnapCenter hypervisor settings for in-guest mounts
description: SnapCenter global hypervisor settings are set so that VMs with in-guest NFS or iSCSI mounts no longer produce virtualization warnings.

name: Copy an SAP system
description: A renamed copy of an SAP system with a new SID and instance numbers is provisioned from a Snapshot-based storage clone.

name: Create a virtual machine for SAP HANA
description: A virtual machine for SAP HANA is created with disks on the prepared VMFS datastores.

name: Create a VMFS datastore for SAP HANA
description: VMFS datastores are created on the LUNs that hold the SAP HANA VM files and database files.

name: Create an SAP HANA database clone with SnapCenter
description: SnapCenter creates a storage clone from a Snapshot backup, maps it to the host and attaches it to the target HANA system.

name: Create LVM volume groups and logical volumes for SAP HANA
description: The SAP HANA LUNs are initialized as physical volumes and LVM volume groups and logical volumes are created for the data and log partitions on the hosts.

name: Destroy a cloned SAP system
description: A stopped cloned SAP system is decommissioned and its mount points and storage clones are deleted.

name: Enable disk UUIDs on an SAP HANA virtual machine
description: The disk.EnableUUID parameter is set to TRUE on the SAP HANA VM so that the guest OS sees consistent disk identifiers.

name: Mount SAP HANA NFS file systems
description: The SAP HANA data, log and shared NFS file systems are mounted on the database hosts.

name: Refresh an SAP HANA system
description: An existing SAP HANA target system is refreshed with data from a source system by cloning a Snapshot backup, followed by SAP post-processing.

name: Configure SR-IOV network interfaces for SAP HANA on SUSE KVM
description: SR-IOV virtual functions are created, enabled at boot and assigned to SAP HANA KVM virtual machines for redundant Ethernet networking.

name: Create an SAP HANA backup user and user store key for SnapCenter
description: A database user with backup privileges is created in the SAP HANA system database and an hdbuserstore key is created for SnapCenter access.

name: Install SAP HANA on a multiple-host system
description: SAP HANA software is installed on all worker and standby hosts of a multiple-host system using the SAP installation tool with the storage-specific settings.

name: Configure storage for SAP HANA with FCP
description: The storage system is configured for SAP HANA over Fibre Channel: disk shelves checked, aggregates, SVM, LIFs, volumes, LUNs and initiator groups created.

name: Configure storage for SAP HANA with NFS
description: The storage system is configured for SAP HANA over NFS: disk shelves checked, aggregates, SVM, LIFs, volumes and export access created.

name: Configure an iSCSI NetApp datastore for OpenNebula
description: An OpenNebula NetApp datastore backed by ONTAP over iSCSI is created and usable by all OpenNebula hosts.

name: Configure FC LVM storage for Proxmox VE
description: An ONTAP FC LUN is presented to all Proxmox VE hosts and added as shared LVM storage.

name: Configure FC LVM-thin storage for OpenNebula
description: An ONTAP FC LUN is presented to all OpenNebula hosts and used as an LVM-thin datastore.

name: Configure iSCSI LVM storage for Proxmox VE
description: An ONTAP iSCSI LUN is presented to all Proxmox VE hosts and added as shared LVM storage.

name: Configure iSCSI LVM-thin storage for OpenNebula
description: An ONTAP iSCSI LUN is presented to all OpenNebula hosts and used as an LVM-thin datastore.

name: Configure NVMe/FC LVM storage for Proxmox VE
description: An ONTAP NVMe namespace over NVMe/FC is presented to all Proxmox VE hosts and added as shared LVM storage.

name: Configure NVMe/FC LVM-thin storage for OpenNebula
description: An ONTAP NVMe namespace over NVMe/FC is presented to all OpenNebula hosts and used as an LVM-thin datastore.

name: Configure NVMe/TCP LVM storage for Proxmox VE
description: An ONTAP NVMe namespace over NVMe/TCP is presented to all Proxmox VE hosts and added as shared LVM storage.

name: Configure NVMe/TCP LVM-thin storage for OpenNebula
description: An ONTAP NVMe namespace over NVMe/TCP is presented to all OpenNebula hosts and used as an LVM-thin datastore.

name: Configure the Windows host iSCSI initiator
description: The Windows iSCSI service starts automatically and MPIO claims iSCSI devices.

name: Create an SVM and LIFs for iSCSI datastores in VCF
description: An SVM with iSCSI enabled and iSCSI LIFs is available for VCF VMFS or vVols datastores.

name: Create an SVM, LIFs and NVMe namespace for NVMe/TCP datastores in VCF
description: An SVM with NVMe/TCP LIFs and an NVMe namespace is available for VCF workload domain datastores.

name: Provision an iSCSI LUN for Hyper-V
description: An iSCSI LUN is created on an ONTAP SVM and mapped to the Hyper-V hosts.

name: Configure vMSC non-uniform host access with SnapMirror active sync
description: vSphere hosts in each fault domain access only their local ONTAP array in a SnapMirror active sync metro cluster.

name: Configure vMSC uniform host access with SnapMirror active sync
description: vSphere hosts access both fault-domain ONTAP arrays in a SnapMirror active sync metro cluster set up with ONTAP tools.

name: Create a Microsoft stretch failover cluster
description: A multi-site Microsoft Hyper-V stretch failover cluster with MPIO for iSCSI is built across both sites.

name: Fail back OpenShift Virtualization VMs after disaster recovery
description: Failed-over VMs are returned to the original cluster by reverse-resyncing the replication relationship.

name: Fail over OpenShift Virtualization VMs without a site outage
description: The AppMirror relationship is promoted so VMs run on the target cluster.

name: Implement disaster recovery for VCF with NetApp Disaster Recovery
description: VCF workloads are protected and recoverable using the NetApp Disaster Recovery service in the NetApp Console.

name: Install and configure ONTAP Mediator
description: ONTAP Mediator is installed, verified and its certificate installed on the clusters for SnapMirror active sync.

name: Set up the target cluster for OpenShift Virtualization disaster recovery
description: The destination OpenShift cluster has an AppVault and namespace ready to receive failed-over VMs.

name: Limit the maximum size of volumes created by Trident
description: SVM storage limits and Trident backend volume size limits cap the size of volumes Trident can create.

name: Migrate VMs to Amazon EC2 with FSx for ONTAP storage
description: VMs are migrated to Amazon EC2 with their data on FSx for ONTAP iSCSI LUNs using Cirrus Data MigrateOps, and the result is verified.

name: Review requirements for migrating VMs to Amazon EC2 with FSx for ONTAP
description: Describes the goals and requirements of migrating VMs to Amazon EC2 with FSx for ONTAP.

name: Add a storage system to SnapCenter Plug-in for VMware vSphere
description: An ONTAP storage system is registered in SnapCenter Plug-in for VMware vSphere so its datastores and VMs can be protected.

name: Add Proxmox Backup Server to a Proxmox VE cluster
description: A Proxmox Backup Server is added as backup storage to the Proxmox VE datacenter.

name: Back up a SnapCenter Plug-in for VMware vSphere resource group
description: An on-demand backup of a resource group is taken with a selected policy.

name: Back up and restore OpenShift Virtualization VMs with NetApp Backup and Recovery
description: OpenShift Virtualization VMs are backed up to an object storage target and restored using the NetApp Console Backup and Recovery service.

name: Back up Proxmox VE VMs to Proxmox Backup Server
description: A backup of a Proxmox VE VM or container is written to a Proxmox Backup Server datastore on ONTAP storage.

name: Back up Proxmox VE VMs with Storage Manager for Proxmox
description: A crash- or file-consistent ONTAP snapshot backup of a Proxmox VE VM is created with Storage Manager for Proxmox.

name: Clone Proxmox VE VMs with Storage Manager for Proxmox
description: A VM clone is created on a chosen node from an ONTAP snapshot with Storage Manager for Proxmox.

name: Configure a Proxmox Backup Server datastore on ONTAP storage
description: A Proxmox Backup Server datastore is created on an ONTAP LUN, NVMe namespace or NFS export and mounted persistently.

name: Configure SnapMirror disaster recovery for a Proxmox Backup Server datastore
description: The Proxmox Backup Server datastore volume is replicated with SnapMirror so a secondary PBS can mount it after a disaster.

name: Configure third-party backup for Hyper-V VMs
description: A third-party backup solution is configured with the ONTAP array to protect and restore Hyper-V VMs using storage snapshots.

name: Create a Proxmox Backup Server sync job to ONTAP S3 storage
description: A local sync job copies backups from a Proxmox Backup Server datastore to an ONTAP S3 datastore.

name: Create a Storage Manager for Proxmox backup policy
description: A backup policy that schedules and retains VM backups is created in Storage Manager for Proxmox.

name: Create an on-demand backup of an OpenShift Virtualization VM with Velero
description: An on-demand backup of a VM's metadata and disks is created with OADP/Velero.

name: Deploy SnapCenter Plug-in for VMware vSphere
description: The SnapCenter Plug-in for VMware vSphere appliance is deployed from its OVA and accessible in the vSphere Client.

name: Install the OpenShift API for Data Protection operator
description: The OADP operator is installed and configured with an object storage backup location.

name: Protect OpenShift Virtualization VMs with volume group snapshots
description: Multi-disk OpenShift Virtualization VMs are protected with crash-consistent Trident volume group snapshots.

name: Protect VMs on a vVols datastore with SnapCenter Plug-in for VMware vSphere
description: VMs on a vVols datastore are backed up by registering storage, creating a policy and a resource group in SnapCenter Plug-in for VMware vSphere.

name: Recover Hyper-V VMs at the secondary site from SnapMirror
description: The SnapMirror relationship is broken and the replicated LUNs are mapped and brought online for the secondary Hyper-V cluster.

name: Restore Proxmox VE VMs and containers from Proxmox Backup Server
