description: The IP addresses of every node in the grid are changed together using the Change IP tool.

name: Change the LACP PDU rate
description: The LACP PDU rate used on bonded ports of grid nodes is checked and changed temporarily.

name: Change the MTU setting of an appliance
description: Change the MTU for the appliance's Grid, Admin and Client Networks.

name: Check the DNS server configuration of an appliance
description: Check the appliance's temporary DNS server settings in the StorageGRID Appliance Installer and change them if needed.

name: Configure a load balancer health monitor for an S3 bucket
description: Create an F5 BIG-IP local traffic manager monitor that checks StorageGRID S3 health through a bucket request.

name: Configure a storage proxy
description: Enable and configure a forward proxy that Storage Nodes use for outbound traffic, such as traffic to Cloud Storage Pools.

name: Configure appliance IP addresses
description: Assign static or DHCP IP addresses, routes and MTU for the appliance on the Grid, Admin, and Client networks.

name: Configure storage controller management IP addresses
description: Set the IPv4 or IPv6 management addresses that the appliance's storage controllers use to reach SANtricity System Manager.

name: Configure the admin proxy
description: Admin Nodes send outbound management traffic through the configured proxy server.

name: Configure the host network for Linux deployments
description: Configure Linux host network interfaces, such as an LACP bond carrying VLAN interfaces, for StorageGRID node networks.

name: Configure the network link settings of an appliance
description: Set an appliance's port link speed, port bond mode, network bond mode, VLAN tagging and enabled networks from Configure Networking > Link Configuration in the StorageGRID Appliance Installer.

name: Create a high availability group
description: Create a StorageGRID high availability (HA) group: enter details, add interfaces, enter virtual IP addresses and set the priority order.

name: Create a load balancer endpoint
description: Create a StorageGRID load balancer endpoint: enter endpoint details, select a binding mode and attach a certificate.

name: Create a traffic classification policy
description: Create a StorageGRID traffic classification policy to identify and limit network traffic.

name: Create a VLAN interface
description: Create a StorageGRID VLAN interface: enter details, choose parent interfaces and confirm the settings.

name: Delete a DNS server
description: A DNS server is removed from the grid's DNS server list.

name: Delete a Grid Network subnet
description: A subnet is removed from the Grid Network subnet list.

name: Delete a traffic classification policy
description: Delete a traffic classification policy that is no longer needed.

name: Edit a high availability group
description: The name, interfaces, priority or virtual IP addresses of an HA group are changed.

name: Enable CORS for a management interface
description: Cross-origin requests from specified domains are allowed to the Grid Manager or Tenant Manager.

name: Learn about source client IP visibility through load balancers
description: Describes how preserving the client source IP through a load balancer allows it to be recorded in audit logs and used in aws:SourceIp policies.

name: Modify a DNS server
description: An existing DNS server entry in the grid's DNS server list is changed.

name: Modify a Grid Network subnet
description: An existing subnet in the Grid Network subnet list is changed.

name: Modify a traffic classification policy
description: Edit the name, description, matching rules or limits of a traffic classification policy.

name: Modify a VLAN interface
description: Edit a VLAN interface's VLAN ID, description or parent interfaces.

name: Modify DNS configuration for a single grid node
description: A single grid node gets a custom DNS nameserver and search domain configuration that differs from the grid-wide settings.

name: Modify link costs
description: Set the link cost values between sites to influence how data is routed across the grid.

name: Modify the Admin Network subnet list
description: Subnets are added to, changed in or deleted from the Admin Network subnet list of one or more nodes using the Change IP tool.

name: Relocate a grid site and change site networking
description: Relocate a site by staging Grid IP changes, changing appliance VLANs and applying the site-wide network change.

name: Remap appliance network ports
description: Remap inbound or outbound TCP or UDP ports on an appliance network to work around port conflicts or firewall constraints.

name: Remove a high availability group
description: HA groups that are not used by load balancer endpoints are removed.

name: Remove a VLAN interface
description: Remove one or more VLAN interfaces.

name: Remove port remaps
description: Port remaps configured on a node are removed so that the default ports are restored.

name: Restore network connectivity for isolated nodes
description: Grid nodes that became isolated after IP address changes regain network connectivity with the rest of the grid.

name: Set the BMC management port IP address
description: Set a static or DHCP IP address for the appliance's BMC management port.

name: Update MAC address references for an appliance
description: Work out the appliance's network MAC addresses from its BMC label and update the DNS and network references that use them.

name: Verify appliance network connectivity
description: Ping a host on the Grid, Admin, or Client network from the appliance, and optionally test the MTU across the whole path, to confirm connectivity.

name: Verify port-level network connectivity
description: Test that the appliance can reach specified TCP or UDP ports on hosts in a StorageGRID network, so that no firewall is blocking them.

name: View IP addresses of a grid node
description: Display the IP addresses assigned to a grid node from its Nodes overview page.

name: Add an S3 endpoint domain name
description: Add S3 endpoint domain names so the grid can support S3 virtual-hosted-style requests.

name: Browse and manage objects in a bucket
description: Objects in an S3 bucket are viewed and managed directly from the tenant's bucket details page.

name: Change bucket consistency
description: Change the consistency level that applies to operations on the objects in an S3 bucket.

name: Change object versioning for a bucket
description: Set the object versioning state of an S3 bucket to enabled, suspended or disabled.

name: Configure a global namespace for grid federation
description: Tenants can access buckets across multiple federated StorageGRID systems through a global namespace.

name: Configure event notifications
description: Enable event notifications on a source bucket so that object events are sent to a platform services endpoint.

name: Configure S3 regions
description: Define the S3 regions and the default region available to buckets and ILM rules.

name: Configure StorageGRID for S3 client connections
description: Set up S3 client access end to end by creating an HA group, a load balancer endpoint, a tenant account, and a bucket with access keys, either with the S3 setup wizard or manually.

name: Configure the search integration service
description: Enable search integration on a bucket so that object metadata is sent to an Elasticsearch platform services endpoint.

name: Create a branch bucket
description: Create a branch bucket from a base bucket, optionally setting S3 Object Lock, default retention, a capacity limit and an object count limit.

name: Create a bucket
description: Create an S3 bucket with a name and region, optionally enabling versioning, S3 Object Lock, default retention and capacity or object count limits.

name: Create a platform services endpoint
description: Create a platform services endpoint with a display name, URI, URN, authentication and server verification settings.

name: Create a tenant account
description: Create a StorageGRID tenant account: enter details, select permissions and define root access.

name: Create an S3 bucket and access keys for FabricPool
description: In the Tenant Manager, create an S3 bucket for FabricPool data and an access key pair that ONTAP will use.

name: Delete a bucket
description: Delete one or more empty S3 buckets.

name: Delete a platform services endpoint
description: Delete one or more platform services endpoints.

name: Delete an S3 endpoint domain name
description: Delete a configured S3 endpoint domain name.

name: Delete objects in a bucket
description: Delete all objects and object versions from an S3 bucket.

name: Disable CORS for a bucket
description: Turn off Cross-Origin Resource Sharing for an S3 bucket.

name: Enable CORS for a bucket
description: Enable Cross-Origin Resource Sharing on an S3 bucket by supplying a CORS configuration XML.

name: Enable or disable last access time updates for a bucket
description: Turn last access time updates for the objects in an S3 bucket on or off.

name: Modify a platform services endpoint
description: Change the configuration of an existing platform services endpoint.

name: Modify the CORS configuration of a bucket
description: Update the CORS configuration XML of an S3 bucket.

name: Rename an S3 endpoint domain name
description: Change a configured S3 endpoint domain name.

name: Test a platform services endpoint connection
description: Test the connection to a platform services endpoint to confirm that the destination resource exists and can be reached with the configured credentials, including checking whether an endpoint error is still current.

name: Test the S3 REST API configuration
description: Use an S3 client to create a bucket, upload an object and list the bucket contents to confirm S3 REST API access works.

name: View bucket details
description: Review the summary list of S3 buckets and the settings and usage of a specific bucket.

name: Configure S3 Object Lock WORM storage for Enterprise Vault
description: Create an S3 Object Lock bucket with default retention and configure Enterprise Vault to use it as WORM storage.

name: Enable S3 Object Lock
description: Enable S3 Object Lock for the whole grid, optionally allowing it to be enabled on existing buckets.

name: Protect data from ransomware with a replicated versioned bucket
description: Replicate a versioned bucket to a secondary bucket with CloudMirror platform services as a ransomware defense.

name: Update S3 Object Lock default retention for a bucket
description: Enable, disable or change the default retention mode and period for a bucket that uses S3 Object Lock.

name: Add a client certificate
description: Add a client certificate so that external monitoring tools can access Prometheus securely.

name: Approve or reject MAV-protected operation requests
description: Approve or reject pending requests for operations protected by multi-admin verification and review the request history.

name: Change node console passwords
description: Change the node console passwords, using either one global password or unique passwords per node.

name: Change SSH access passwords and keys
description: Rotate the Admin Node SSH access passwords and internal SSH keys, then download the new recovery package.

name: Change the BMC admin or root password
description: Set a new password for the admin or root account of the appliance's BMC interface.

name: Change the password of a tenant's local root user
description: Set a new password for a tenant account's local root user.

name: Change the provisioning passphrase
description: Replace the grid's provisioning passphrase with a new one.

name: Change your Grid Manager password
description: The signed-in local user's Grid Manager password is changed.

name: Clone S3 access keys to another grid
description: Use the Tenant Management API to clone a user's S3 access keys from the source grid to the destination grid.

name: Configure a bucket policy
description: Add, edit or remove the access policy of an S3 bucket.

name: Configure an S3 trust policy for AssumeRole
description: Add an S3 trust policy to a tenant group so that the listed users can perform AssumeRole to get temporary credentials.

name: Configure certificates for FabricPool
description: Certificates for FabricPool connections are configured through the HA group, S3 load balancer endpoint and ONTAP cloud tier attachment.

name: Configure external access ports for the internal firewall
description: External ports on grid nodes are opened or closed according to the internal firewall settings.

name: Configure external SSH access
description: Inbound SSH access to grid nodes is blocked or allowed.

name: Configure identity federation
description: An LDAP identity source is configured, tested and saved so that federated groups and users can be used.

name: Configure multi-admin verification
description: Set up multi-admin verification by creating MAV administrator groups and users, enabling MAV and choosing protected operations.

name: Configure network and object security settings
description: Set network and object security options such as stored object encryption and preventing S3 client modification.

name: Configure single sign-on using OIDC
description: Configure and enable OpenID Connect single sign-on by entering identity provider and client details and testing the configuration.

name: Configure single sign-on using SAML
description: Configure and enable SAML single sign-on by entering identity provider details, setting up relying parties and testing the configuration.

name: Configure the identity provider for OIDC single sign-on
description: Register StorageGRID as an OIDC client application in the identity provider (AD FS, Keycloak, Entra ID, Okta or PingFederate) so OpenID Connect single sign-on can work.

name: Configure the identity provider for SAML single sign-on
description: Register each StorageGRID Admin Node as a relying party or service provider in the identity provider (AD FS, PingFederate or Entra ID) so SAML single sign-on can work.

name: Configure the privileged address list for the internal firewall
description: Specified IP addresses or subnets are granted access to ports that are otherwise closed by the internal firewall.

name: Configure the TLS and SSH policy
description: Review the available TLS and SSH security policies and select the one the grid uses.

name: Configure the untrusted Client Network for nodes
description: Selected nodes accept inbound client traffic on the Client Network only on load balancer endpoint ports.

name: Confirm federated users can sign in
description: Federated users are confirmed to be able to sign in to the Grid Manager and Tenant Manager before SSO is enabled.

name: Create a custom TLS and SSH security policy
description: A custom TLS and SSH policy with the chosen protocols and ciphers is created and applied.

name: Create a local tenant user
description: Create a local user with credentials and assign it to one or more local groups that determine what it can do.

name: Create a tenant group
description: Create a local or federated tenant group and assign its permissions and S3 group policy.

name: Create an admin group
description: Create a local or federated Grid Manager admin group with an access mode, management permissions and, for local groups, member users.

name: Create an admin user
description: Create a local admin user with credentials, access settings and group membership.

name: Create S3 access keys
description: Create an S3 access key pair for yourself or for another tenant user, optionally with an expiration time.

name: Deactivate features
description: Selected features, such as changing the tenant root password, are deactivated through the API.

name: Delete an admin group
description: Selected admin groups are removed.

name: Delete an admin user
description: Delete one or more local admin users.

name: Delete local tenant users
description: Delete one or more local tenant users.

name: Delete S3 access keys
description: Remove one or more S3 access keys that belong to yourself or another tenant user.

name: Delete tenant groups
description: Delete one or more StorageGRID tenant groups.

name: Disable identity federation
description: Identity federation is turned off for the grid or tenant.

name: Disable single sign-on
description: Turn off single sign-on for the grid.

name: Download a client certificate
description: Download or copy a configured client certificate from the Certificates page.

name: Download the Grid CA certificate
description: The Grid CA certificate is copied or downloaded for use by clients.

name: Download the management interface certificate
description: Download or copy the management interface server certificate or its CA bundle.

name: Download the S3 API certificate
description: Download or copy the S3 API server certificate or its CA bundle.

name: Duplicate a local tenant user
description: Create a new local user by copying the settings of an existing local user.

name: Duplicate a tenant group
description: Duplicate an existing StorageGRID tenant group to create a new group with the same settings.

name: Duplicate an admin user
description: Create a new admin user by duplicating an existing user's settings.

name: Import federated users
description: Federated users are imported from the identity source.

name: Modify a client certificate
description: The name, permissions or attached certificate of an existing client certificate is changed.

name: Modify a local tenant user
description: View a local user's details and edit its full name, password, group membership or access keys.

name: Modify a tenant group
description: View and edit the details of a StorageGRID tenant group, such as its name.

name: Modify interface security settings
description: Change interface security settings such as the browser inactivity timeout and the Management API stack trace setting.

name: Reactivate deactivated features
description: Features that were deactivated through the API are reactivated.

name: Remove a client certificate
description: The selected client certificate is deleted.

name: Request approval for a multi-admin verification protected operation
description: A protected operation request is submitted and tracked until other administrators approve it.

name: Restore the default management interface certificate
description: The management interface returns to the default StorageGRID certificate.

name: Restore the default S3 API certificate
description: S3 client connections return to the default StorageGRID S3 API certificate.

name: Restore the default TLS and SSH policy
description: Temporarily revert the grid to the default TLS and SSH cipher configuration from an Admin Node command line so the policy can be configured again.

name: Retry group synchronization
description: Retry syncing federated groups that failed to sync from the identity source, for all groups or one group.

name: Retry user synchronization
description: Retry syncing federated users that failed to sync from the identity source, for all users or one user.

name: Sign out of StorageGRID
description: End the current Grid Manager or API session, including single logout when single sign-on is enabled.

name: Synchronize with the identity source
description: Force an immediate sync of federated groups and users from the configured identity source.

name: Temporarily disable and reenable single sign-on for an Admin Node
description: SSO is temporarily disabled on one Admin Node so local users can sign in, then re-enabled.

name: Update the management interface certificate
description: Install a new management interface certificate on the grid and accept it for the managed StorageGRID system.

name: Use a custom management interface certificate
description: Replace the Grid Manager and Tenant Manager management interface certificate with a custom one. You can upload a CA-signed certificate or generate a self-signed certificate, either in the Grid Manager or with the make-certificate script on the primary Admin Node.

name: Use a custom S3 API certificate
description: A custom certificate is uploaded or generated for S3 client connections to Storage Nodes.

name: View S3 access keys
description: List the S3 access keys of yourself or another tenant user, sorted by expiration time or access key ID.

name: View security certificates
description: Open the Certificates page to review information about each category of security certificate used by the grid.

name: View the management interface certificate status
description: Check whether the management interface certificate of a managed StorageGRID system is approved and valid.

name: Cable an appliance
description: Connect the appliance's BMC management, Grid, Admin, and Client network ports and controller interconnects to the correct networks and devices.

name: Configure iSCSI storage for Linux grid hosts
description: Discover and log in to external iSCSI LUNs and configure multipath devices for use by grid nodes.

name: Configure the container engine storage volume on Linux hosts
description: Create and mount a file system for the container engine storage volume on each Linux host and make the mount persistent.

name: Configure the grid and complete installation
description: Configure a newly deployed grid (license, sites, Grid Network subnets, NTP/DNS, passwords, node approval) and complete the StorageGRID installation, either in the Grid Manager install wizard or with the configure-storagegrid.py automation script.

name: Connect power and power on an appliance
description: Connect the power cords to separate PDUs and apply power so that the appliance and its shelves boot.

name: Create node configuration files
description: Create the node configuration directory and files on each Linux host that describe the grid nodes to deploy.

name: Deploy a services appliance as a Gateway Node or non-primary Admin Node
description: Install StorageGRID on a services appliance so that it joins the grid as a Gateway Node or a non-primary Admin Node.

name: Deploy a services appliance as the primary Admin Node
description: Install StorageGRID on a services appliance so that it becomes the grid's primary Admin Node.

name: Deploy an appliance Storage Node
description: Use the appliance installer to name the node, point it to the primary Admin Node, and start installing StorageGRID as a Storage Node.

name: Deploy grid nodes
description: Deploy StorageGRID grid nodes (for example as VMware vSphere virtual machines, manually or with the OVF Tool script, or on Linux hosts or appliances) for a new installation or to add them to the grid in an expansion.

name: Download and extract StorageGRID installation files
description: Download the installation archive for the running version from the NetApp Support Site and extract it for installation, expansion or node recovery.

name: Install a container engine on Linux hosts
description: Install, enable and start Docker or Podman on the Linux hosts and confirm the installed version.

name: Install an appliance into a cabinet or rack
description: Install rails and slide a StorageGRID appliance or its compute controller into a cabinet or rack.

name: Install drive shelves into a cabinet or rack
description: Mount the appliance's storage controller shelf and expansion drive shelves on rails in a cabinet or rack.

name: Install drives into drive shelves
description: Insert the shipped drives into the drawers of the appliance drive shelves after the shelves are racked.

name: Install Linux on grid hosts
description: Install and prepare Linux on all physical or virtual grid hosts, including repository access and disabling swap.

name: Install StorageGRID host services on Linux
description: Install the StorageGRID RPM or DEB packages on each Linux host.

name: Monitor appliance installation
description: Monitor the progress of StorageGRID software installation on an appliance until it completes.

name: Prepare the site for appliance installation
description: Confirm the site meets environmental, power and rack requirements before installing the appliance.

name: Register appliance hardware
description: Register the appliance chassis serial number on the NetApp Support Site so that it is entitled to support.

name: Set up SANtricity System Manager
description: Access SANtricity System Manager on the appliance's storage controller, set the administrator password and configure hardware alerts.

name: Start the StorageGRID host service on Linux hosts
description: Enable and start the StorageGRID host service on each Linux host and start any grid nodes that are not running.

name: Verify installation file signatures
description: Manually verify the certificate chain and signatures of the downloaded installation archive.

name: Change the appliance RAID mode
description: Before the node is deployed, select a different RAID mode for the appliance's storage to meet storage and recovery requirements.

name: Create a storage pool
description: Create a storage pool from a site and storage grade for use in ILM rules.

name: Create and assign storage grades
description: Custom storage grades are defined and assigned to Storage Nodes for use in storage pools.

name: Modify a storage pool
description: Change a storage pool's name or its sites and storage grades.

name: Remove a storage pool
description: Remove a storage pool that no ILM rule or policy uses.

name: View storage pool details
description: Display a storage pool's Storage Nodes, capacity and ILM usage.

name: Access log files on a grid node
description: Sign in to a grid node over SSH as root to access its StorageGRID log files.

name: Collect log files and system data
description: Gather log files and system data from selected grid nodes for a time range into a downloadable archive.

name: Configure a replacement primary Admin Node
description: Use the installer on the replacement node to recover a failed primary Admin Node from the latest recovery package.

name: Copy audit logs from a failed primary Admin Node
description: Stop the AMS service and preserve the audit log files from a failed primary Admin Node before it is recovered.

name: Copy audit logs to a new or recovered Admin Node
description: Copy historical audit log files onto an Admin Node that lacks them (a new expansion Admin Node or a recovered Admin Node) with scp, and fix their ownership so its audit history matches the rest of the grid.

name: Determine the hotfix requirement for primary Admin Node recovery
description: Check the software version of the primary Admin Node to determine whether a hotfix must be applied to the recovered node.

name: Force a service to terminate
description: A service on a grid node that does not respond to a normal stop is forced to terminate.

name: Identify and unmount failed storage volumes
description: Record the failed storage volumes on a Storage Node and unmount them with the sn-unmount-volume script before recovery.

name: Monitor erasure-coded data repair jobs
description: Check the status of erasure-coded data repair jobs and retry failed repairs.

name: Prepare an appliance for StorageGRID reinstallation
description: Run sgareinstall on the failed appliance node so that StorageGRID software can be reinstalled on it.

name: Recover an orphaned node on a Linux host
description: Restore a node reported as orphaned on a Linux host by checking logs, restarting the node and restarting the container engine.

name: Recover failed storage volumes and rebuild the Cassandra database
description: Replace and reformat failed storage volumes on a Storage Node whose system drive is intact and rebuild its Cassandra database.

name: Remount and reformat Storage Node storage volumes
description: Run the recovery scripts on a recovered Storage Node to remount properly formatted storage volumes and reformat the others.

name: Replace a failed grid node for recovery
description: Replace the host of a failed grid node so that node recovery can proceed, by deploying a recovery VMware VM, restoring the node onto a replacement Linux host, or installing a services appliance under the failed node's name.

name: Replace a software-based node with a services appliance
description: Replace a failed VMware or Linux grid node with a services appliance installed under the failed node's name and complete node recovery.

name: Resolve the Grid Network MTU mismatch alert
description: Compare eth0 MTU settings across all nodes and correct mismatched values.

name: Resolve the low metadata storage alert
description: Investigate a Low metadata storage alert and add Storage Nodes through an expansion when metadata space is running out.

name: Resolve the low object data storage alert
description: Investigate a low object data storage alert on a Storage Node and plan an expansion to add capacity.

name: Resolve the node network reception frame error alert
description: Investigate and correct the causes of network frame reception errors on a node, such as FEC or switch port mismatches.

name: Resolve the objects potentially lost alert
description: Investigate objects reported as potentially lost using Node object counts and the audit log, and attempt recovery.

name: Resolve the S3 PUT object size too large alert
description: Identify the tenant sending single PutObject requests larger than 5 GiB and tell them to use multipart upload.

name: Resolve the watermark override alert
description: Check object data usage and the optimized watermark values to decide whether custom storage volume watermarks can be replaced.

name: Restore object data to a storage volume or Storage Node
description: Restore lost replicated or erasure-coded object data to recovered storage volumes or nodes, either through automatic restore mode or by starting restoration manually.

name: Restore the Admin Node database on a recovered Admin Node
description: Copy the Admin Node database from a healthy source Admin Node to a recovered Admin Node to preserve historical attribute and audit information.

name: Run an object existence check
description: Create and run a job that verifies that expected object data exists on selected Storage Node volumes.

name: Run diagnostics
description: Run the built-in diagnostics and review their status, related Grafana charts and Prometheus expressions.

name: Send an AutoSupport package manually
description: Manually trigger an AutoSupport package to be sent to technical support.

name: Set a Storage Node's storage state online after recovery
description: Check a recovered Storage Node's storage state and change it to Online if it is Read-only or Offline.

name: Start recovery of a failed grid node
description: Select the pending replacement node on the node recovery page, enter the provisioning passphrase and start recovery.

name: Start StorageGRID installation on a replacement appliance
description: Use the appliance installer to connect a replacement appliance to the primary Admin Node with the failed node's name and start the StorageGRID installation.

name: Troubleshoot a hardware setup that appears to hang
description: Use seven-segment display codes, LEDs, and boot-up and error codes to diagnose an appliance hardware setup that appears to be stuck.

name: Troubleshoot a service in an error state
description: Diagnose and recover a StorageGRID grid node service that is in an error state.

name: Troubleshoot Admin Node sign-in errors
description: Diagnose sign-in failures to the Grid Manager by checking other Admin Nodes, node hardware and services, and SSO configuration.

name: Troubleshoot alert email notifications
description: Diagnose why alert notification emails are not received by checking email settings, spam filters and mail transfer.

name: Troubleshoot appliance connection issues
description: Find out why the appliance or its appliance installer cannot be reached, by pinging it, checking the IP address, cabling, and transceivers, and using a direct connection.

name: Troubleshoot certificate errors
description: Check certificate validity and trust settings and replace expired or invalid certificates to resolve certificate errors.

name: Troubleshoot error synchronizing with SANtricity OS
description: Resolve an HE error when the compute controller cannot synchronize with SANtricity OS, by checking or replacing the SAS interconnect cables.

name: Troubleshoot expansion shelves missing from the appliance installer
description: Find out why expansion shelves are missing from the appliance installer by checking their cabling and power.

name: Troubleshoot grid expansion errors
description: Connect to a failed expansion node and collect the installation logs needed to diagnose expansion errors.

name: Troubleshoot installation issues
description: Diagnose and fix problems that prevent grid nodes from installing or starting, such as insufficient virtual machine resources.

name: Troubleshoot IPv6 support on a Linux host
description: Check whether IPv6 is disabled on the Linux host and node container, enable it and restart the node.

name: Troubleshoot multi-admin verification email notifications
description: Diagnose why multi-admin verification email notifications are not being received.

name: Troubleshoot platform services endpoint errors
description: Find a platform services endpoint error on the endpoint details page and fix it by correcting the endpoint configuration and retesting the connection.

name: Troubleshoot user interface issues
description: Resolve Grid Manager or Tenant Manager display issues by using a supported browser and clearing the browser cache.

name: View appliance boot-up codes
description: View the controller's boot-up codes through a VGA console, the BMC KVM, or a serial terminal to diagnose installation problems.

name: View appliance error codes
description: View the controller's current and previous error codes through the serial port or the BMC to diagnose hardware installation failures.

name: View appliance status indicators and codes
description: Reference describing the appliance's indicators, buttons, SSD LEDs and boot-up codes used to determine component status.

name: Add storage volumes to a Storage Node
description: Add new storage volumes (object stores) to an existing Storage Node to increase its storage capacity.

name: Apply a hotfix
description: Upload and apply a hotfix to the grid nodes.

name: Check grid health before a software update
description: Confirm that all grid nodes are connected, alerts are resolved and no other maintenance is running before upgrading or applying a hotfix.

name: Clone an appliance node
description: Clone a source StorageGRID appliance node onto a new target appliance so the target takes over the node's identity and data.

name: Configure newly added nodes and sites
description: Complete the integration and configuration tasks required for sites, Storage Nodes, Gateway Nodes or Admin Nodes added in an expansion.

name: Decommission a site
description: A data center site and all its nodes are removed from the grid after ILM policies and rules are revised to stop referring to it.

name: Decommission grid nodes
description: The selected grid nodes are permanently removed from the grid, whether they are connected or disconnected.

name: Download a hotfix file
description: Download the required StorageGRID hotfix file from the NetApp Support Site.

name: Download and install StorageGRID packages on Linux hosts for an upgrade
description: Download the upgrade and Linux archives, install the new RPM or DEB packages on all Linux hosts, and remove archives and container images of previous versions.

name: Estimate the upgrade duration
description: Calculate how long upgrading all grid nodes will take, including extra time for Linux nodes.

name: Expand a grid by adding grid nodes or a site
description: New grid nodes are added to an existing site, or a new site is added, so the grid gains capacity or capabilities.

name: Migrate a grid node to a new Linux host
description: A grid node is exported from its source Linux host, imported on a target host and started there.

name: Pause and resume a Storage Node decommission
description: A Storage Node decommission in progress is paused so that another maintenance procedure can run, then resumed.

name: Upgrade drive firmware
description: Upgrade the firmware of the drives in a StorageGRID storage appliance using SANtricity System Manager.

name: Upgrade SANtricity OS on storage controllers
description: Upgrade SANtricity OS on the storage controllers of a StorageGRID appliance, using Grid Manager or maintenance mode.

name: Upgrade StorageGRID software
description: Upload the upgrade files, run prechecks, upgrade the primary Admin Node and then the other grid nodes, and complete the upgrade.

name: Verify and upgrade the appliance installer version
description: Confirm that the appliance installer firmware matches the grid's software version, and upgrade it if it is older.

name: Verify that new Storage Nodes are active after an expansion
description: Confirm that Storage Nodes added in an expansion are storing object data.

name: Verify the installed software version before upgrading
description: Check that the installed StorageGRID version meets the minimum required for the upgrade and apply a hotfix if it does not.

name: Enable automated failover of stateful applications
description: A NodeHealthCheck is configured so that stateful workloads are failed over automatically when a worker node fails.

name: Assign an Autogrow Policy to a storage class
description: A storage class is annotated with an Autogrow Policy so its volumes expand automatically.

name: Create an Autogrow Policy
description: A TridentAutogrowPolicy is created to define automatic volume expansion rules.

name: Delete an Autogrow Policy
description: An Autogrow Policy is deleted after it is removed from the volumes that use it.

name: Expand a persistent volume
description: The size of a Trident-provisioned persistent volume is increased by editing its PVC.

name: Modify an Autogrow Policy
description: The settings of an existing Autogrow Policy are changed.

name: Clone an application to a different cluster
description: Create a copy of a Trident Protect-managed application on another cluster by backing it up and restoring the backup on the destination cluster.

name: Clone an application within the same cluster
description: An application is copied to another namespace on the same cluster by taking a snapshot or backup and restoring it there.

name: Create a mirrored PVC
description: A PVC on a primary cluster is replicated with SnapMirror to a secondary PVC through TridentMirrorRelationship CRs.

name: Create a protection schedule
description: A schedule is created to take application snapshots and backups automatically.

name: Create a volume group snapshot
description: A crash-consistent snapshot of a group of labeled PVCs is created.

name: Create a volume snapshot
description: A VolumeSnapshotClass is defined and a CSI snapshot of an existing PVC is taken.

name: Create an application backup
description: An on-demand Trident Protect backup of an application is created in an AppVault.

name: Create an application snapshot
description: An on-demand Trident Protect snapshot of an application is created.

name: Create an execution hook
description: A Trident Protect execution hook is created to run custom actions around data protection operations.

name: Define a Trident Protect application for virtual machines
description: An application CR is scoped to KubeVirt virtual machines so they can be protected by Trident Protect.

name: Define an application for Trident Protect
description: An application CR is defined so that Trident Protect can manage and protect the application's resources.

name: Delete an application replication relationship
description: The AppMirrorRelationship is deleted, which ends the application's replication.

name: Fail back an application to the original source cluster
description: A failed-over application is returned to its original source cluster by a reverse resync followed by a reversal of the replication direction.

name: Fail over an application to the destination cluster
description: A replicated application is promoted and brought online on the destination cluster.

name: Import a volume snapshot
description: An existing backend snapshot is imported into Kubernetes as a VolumeSnapshot.

name: Migrate an application to a different storage class
description: An application's data is moved to a different storage class by restoring a snapshot with a storage class mapping.

name: Promote a secondary PVC during a planned failover
description: The secondary PVC of a mirror relationship is promoted to read-write after a final snapshot is replicated.

name: Re-establish a PVC mirror relationship after failover
description: A TridentMirrorRelationship that was broken by a failover is re-established.

name: Recover Trident from a replicated etcd backup
description: The Kubernetes cluster and Trident resources are restored from the etcd backup replicated to the destination SVM.

name: Recover Trident volumes after an SVM disaster recovery failover
description: After SVM DR activation, Trident backends are updated to the destination SVM so applications can use the recovered volumes.

name: Remove an AppVault
description: An AppVault object that references an object storage bucket is removed.

name: Replicate a primary PVC to a new secondary PVC
description: An existing mirror relationship is removed and the primary PVC is replicated to a new secondary PVC.

name: Replicate the Kubernetes etcd backup for Trident disaster recovery
description: The Kubernetes etcd backup holding Trident metadata is stored on a replicated FlexVol volume for disaster recovery.

name: Restore a volume in place from a snapshot
description: A PVC is reverted in place to the state captured in one of its volume snapshots.

name: Restore an application from a backup to a different cluster
description: An application is recreated on a different cluster from a backup in a shared AppVault.

name: Restore an application from a backup to a different namespace
description: An application is restored from a Trident Protect backup into a different namespace.

name: Restore an application from a backup to the original namespace
description: An application is restored in place in its original namespace from a Trident Protect backup.

name: Restore an application from a snapshot to a different namespace
description: An application is restored from a Trident Protect snapshot into a different namespace.

name: Restore an application from a snapshot to the original namespace
description: An application is restored in place in its original namespace from a Trident Protect snapshot.

name: Resync a failed-over application replication relationship
description: After a failover, replication resumes from the original source, discarding changes made on the destination.

name: Reverse resync a failed-over application replication relationship
description: After a failover, the failed-over application becomes the source and replicates back to the original source cluster.

name: Reverse the application replication direction
description: Replication direction is swapped by taking a shutdown snapshot on the source and failing over to the other cluster.

name: Set up an application replication relationship
description: An application is replicated to a destination cluster with SnapMirror through an AppMirrorRelationship.

name: View AppVault contents
description: The backups, snapshots and paths stored in an AppVault are listed.

name: View the status of a restore operation
description: The progress and state of a Trident Protect restore operation are displayed.

name: Enable expansion of LUKS-encrypted volumes
description: The feature gate and storage class parameters are set so that LUKS-encrypted volumes can be expanded.

name: Enable LUKS encryption for Trident volumes
description: Volumes provisioned from selected storage pools are encrypted on the host with LUKS using a passphrase secret.

name: Rotate a LUKS passphrase
description: The LUKS passphrase of an encrypted volume is replaced with a new one.

name: Enable secure SMB for Trident volumes
description: SMB volumes provisioned by Trident get share access controlled by specified Active Directory users.

name: Prepare a backend for SMB volume provisioning
description: The ONTAP SMB share and backend settings are set up so Trident can provision SMB volumes.

name: Install FC tools on a Docker host
description: The FC and multipathing packages that Trident for Docker needs are installed and enabled on the host.

name: Configure monitoring for Trident
description: Prometheus collects Trident metrics so they can be queried and monitored.

name: Configure monitoring for Trident Protect
description: Monitoring tools and alerts are set up to track the state of Trident Protect resources.

name: View Trident Protect CLI help
description: Usage guidance for tridentctl-protect commands is displayed.

name: Authenticate Trident to a backend SVM with Active Directory credentials
description: The SVM is joined to Active Directory and the Trident backend uses AD user credentials.

name: Configure certificate-based authentication for a Trident backend
description: Trident authenticates to the ONTAP backend with a client certificate instead of a password.

name: Configure Trident Protect authorization and access control
description: Kubernetes RBAC limits which users or groups can manage Trident Protect resources in each namespace.

name: Create a custom ONTAP role for Trident
description: A least-privilege ONTAP role is created and mapped to the user Trident uses to access the storage system.

name: Customize Trident Protect installation settings
description: Additional Trident Protect Helm chart settings are applied to the installation.

name: Customize Trident Protect security context constraints
description: The OpenShift security context constraints used by Trident Protect are customized.

name: Deploy a volume snapshot controller
description: The volume snapshot CRDs and snapshot controller are deployed on the Kubernetes cluster.

name: Deploy Trident for Docker
description: Trident is configured and started on a Docker host so it can provision Docker volumes.

name: Enable command auto-completion for the Trident Protect CLI
description: Shell auto-completion is enabled for tridentctl-protect commands.

name: Install the Trident Protect CLI plugin
description: The tridentctl-protect CLI plugin is downloaded and installed on a workstation.

name: Install Trident
description: Trident is installed on a Kubernetes cluster so it can provision persistent storage.

name: Install Trident Protect
description: Trident Protect is installed on the Kubernetes cluster with Helm.

name: Restrict Trident Protect pods to specific nodes
description: Trident Protect pods are scheduled only on nodes with specified labels.

name: Run multiple Trident for Docker instances
description: Several Trident instances run on one Docker host, each with its own alias and configuration.

name: Set Trident Protect container resource limits
description: CPU and memory limits are set for Trident Protect containers.

name: Clone a volume across namespaces
description: A volume in a source namespace is made available to a destination namespace through a TridentVolumeReference and a new PVC.

name: Configure topology-aware volume provisioning
description: Topology-aware backends and storage classes are set up so volumes are provisioned in the correct zones or regions.

name: Create a storage class
description: A Kubernetes StorageClass that maps to Trident backends is created for dynamic provisioning.

name: Create a Trident backend
description: A storage backend is defined in Trident so it can provision volumes from the storage system.

name: Import a volume
description: An existing storage volume is imported into Kubernetes as a Trident-managed PVC.

name: Modify the state of a Trident backend
description: A backend's user state is changed, for example suspended so that no new volumes are provisioned from it.

name: Move a backend from TridentBackendConfig to tridentctl management
description: A backend created with a TridentBackendConfig CR is released so that it is managed with tridentctl.

name: Move a backend from tridentctl to TridentBackendConfig management
description: A backend created with tridentctl is brought under management of a TridentBackendConfig CR.

name: Provision a volume with a persistent volume claim
description: A PVC is created so Trident provisions a persistent volume, which is then mounted in a pod.

name: Collect Trident for Docker logs
description: Trident for Docker logs are gathered, with debug logging turned on when needed, for troubleshooting.

name: Generate a Trident Protect support bundle
description: A Trident Protect support bundle is generated, monitored until complete and copied to the local system.

name: Convert a tridentctl installation to an operator-managed installation
description: A Trident instance installed with tridentctl is upgraded and brought under management of the Trident operator.

name: Switch to the OpenShift certified Trident operator
description: An existing Trident installation is removed so that Trident can be reinstalled with the OpenShift certified operator.

name: Uninstall Trident
description: Trident is removed from the Kubernetes cluster.

name: Uninstall Trident for Docker
description: The Trident Docker plugin is disabled and removed after its volumes are removed.

name: Uninstall Trident Protect
description: Trident Protect, its CRs and its namespace are removed from the cluster.

name: Upgrade Trident
description: An existing Trident installation is upgraded to a newer release.

name: Upgrade Trident for Docker
description: The Trident Docker plugin is disabled, upgraded and enabled again.

name: Upgrade Trident Protect
description: Trident Protect is upgraded to a newer version with Helm.

name: Run Codebox-generated automation code
description: Take the code that Codebox generates for an operation defined in the console and run it outside Workload Factory, as AWS CLI commands, a CloudFormation stack, REST API calls or a Terraform script.

name: View the API request of an operation
description: From Tracker, show the API request that was sent for a selected task.

name: Associate an existing link with a file system
description: Associate an FSx for ONTAP file system with a link that already exists in the account.

name: Create a link to a file system
description: Create a new Lambda link and associate it with an FSx for ONTAP file system so Workload Factory can connect to it.

name: Remove a link
description: Remove a link from the Workload Factory account.

name: View links
description: List the links in the account, the file systems associated with each, and each link's ARN.

name: Close CloudShell session tabs
description: Close one CloudShell session tab, all other tabs or all tabs.

name: Configure AI feature settings
description: Choose how Workload Factory AI features use Amazon Bedrock (NetApp-managed, your own account via IAM permissions and an inference profile ARN, or turned off) and save the preference.

name: Deploy a CloudShell session
description: Open a CloudShell session with selected credentials and region to issue AWS or ONTAP CLI commands from Workload Factory.

name: Duplicate a CloudShell session tab
description: Create a copy of an existing CloudShell session tab.

name: Log in to Workload Factory
description: Sign in and open Workload Factory, either directly in the Workload Factory console or through Workloads in the NetApp Console.

name: Modify CloudShell session settings
description: Change the font size and output type of a CloudShell session and apply the settings.

name: Rename a CloudShell session tab
description: Give a CloudShell session tab a new name.

name: Split CloudShell session tabs
description: Drag and drop CloudShell session tabs to show several sessions side by side or stacked in the CloudShell window.

name: Change custom dashboard visibility
description: Change who can see a custom dashboard.

name: Configure notifications
description: Enable one or more Workload Factory notification types, send a test notification and apply the configuration.

name: Create a custom dashboard
description: Create a new custom dashboard by describing in the AI dialog what you want to monitor.

name: Delete a custom dashboard
description: Remove a custom dashboard from the Custom dashboards page.

name: Filter Amazon SNS notifications
description: Apply a JSON message-attribute filter policy to the SNS topic subscription so only selected Workload Factory notifications are delivered.

name: View custom dashboards
description: Open the Custom dashboards catalog and review the list of available dashboards.

name: View operations in Tracker
description: Open Tracker and filter, search or download a report of the jobs run in Workload Factory.

name: Add AWS credentials
description: Add AWS credentials (an IAM role) to the Workload Factory account, either manually or through an AWS CloudFormation stack.

name: Authenticate a link
description: Set the credentials a link uses for a file system, either a Workload Factory password or an AWS Secrets Manager secret ARN.

name: Create a service account
description: Create a named service account in Workload Factory.

name: Delete a service account
description: Permanently delete a service account from Workload Factory.

name: Describe the AWS credential flow
description: Explains how Workload Factory stores the IAM role ARN and external ID at setup and obtains cached, short-lived AWS STS credentials for each API operation.

name: Onboard to Workload Factory securely
description: Choose an onboarding posture, set up AWS trust and least-privilege permissions, and configure connectivity and VPC boundaries before using Workload Factory.

name: Remove AWS credentials
description: Remove stored AWS credentials from the Workload Factory account.

name: Update the link authentication password
description: Replace the password that a link uses to authenticate to an FSx for ONTAP file system.

name: Sign up for Workload Factory
description: Create a Workload Factory login using a NetApp Support Site account or a new NetApp cloud login.

name: Edit and retry a failed operation
description: From Tracker, open a failed operation's page, change its parameters and run it again.

name: Retry a failed operation
description: From Tracker, rerun a failed operation with its original parameters.

name: Analyze capacity trends and decision points
description: Review a file system's historical SSD usage graph over selected time ranges and inspect recommendation or automation decision points.

name: Bulk edit capacity and throughput management settings
description: Change the SSD capacity management or throughput management mode and parameters for several selected file systems at once.

name: Configure SSD capacity management for a file system
description: Enable SSD capacity management for a file system, choose its management mode and set its parameters.

name: Configure throughput management for a file system
description: Enable throughput management for one or more file systems, choose the management mode and set its parameters.

name: View and apply capacity or throughput recommendations
description: Review a file system's SSD capacity or throughput recommendation and its graph, then apply it.

name: Create a snapshot of an EDA project
description: Capture a point-in-time snapshot version of an EDA project.

name: Create an EDA project
description: Add a new CI/CD project in Workload Factory for EDA.

name: Create an EDA workspace
description: Create a Perforce workspace based on a project snapshot, working from Perforce and Workload Factory.

name: Delete an EDA project
description: Remove an existing EDA project from Workload Factory for EDA.

name: Integrate Workload Factory for EDA with Perforce
description: Import the Workload Factory P4V integration file into Perforce P4V so that EDA workflows can be used from within Perforce.

name: Modify an EDA project
description: Edit the settings of an existing EDA project from the Projects page.

name: View a project's workspaces
description: Display the workspaces that belong to a selected EDA project.

name: View EDA projects
description: List and review the existing EDA projects on the Projects page.

name: Activate the Overview dashboard
description: Activate the Overview dashboard, adding credentials if needed, so that metrics collection begins for the FSx for ONTAP file systems.

name: Analyze volume latency trends
description: Use the detailed latency charts, filtered by time frame and read/write type, to find patterns in volume latency over time and track whether remediation worked.

name: Configure custom filters for the Projects dashboard
description: Define custom filters so the Projects dashboard organizes metrics by business structure such as projects, teams or applications.

name: Configure latency monitoring thresholds
description: Set or edit the latency threshold values that determine when latency events are raised for FSx for ONTAP volumes.

name: Filter the EDA dashboard
description: Apply available filters to narrow the dashboard data to selected projects, teams or other criteria.

name: View cluster health status
description: Review the health status of the FSx for ONTAP file systems, including latency events and ONTAP events, from the Overview dashboard.

name: View file systems
description: List FSx for ONTAP file systems with their SSD usage and throughput usage, and search, sort, customize columns or export the list to CSV.

name: View latency events
description: Review the latency events table that lists volumes with latency above the configured thresholds.

name: View project volume usage metrics
description: Review capacity and performance metrics for project volumes in the Projects dashboard, either aggregated across all volumes or per individual volume.

name: Clone an EDA project
description: Create a clone of an EDA project from one of its versions.

name: Analyze a latency event
description: Open a latency event's analysis panel and use the basic component breakdown and optional AI analysis to find the root cause.

name: Collect and upload VM inventory data
description: Capture VM configuration and performance data from vCenter with RVTools, the migration advisor VM collector script or Data Infrastructure Insights, and upload it to Workload Factory as a VM inventory dataset for migration planning.

name: Create a migration deployment plan
description: Create a deployment (migration) plan for moving on-premises VMware workloads to a cloud target, either with the migration advisor from a VM inventory dataset or by manually entering the VM environment requirements.

name: Create a migration plan report
description: Generate a PDF or CSV report that documents a saved migration plan.

name: Delete a migration plan
description: Remove a saved migration plan from the VMware planning center.

name: Delete a VM inventory dataset
description: Remove an uploaded VM inventory dataset from the VMware planning center.

name: Deploy the FSx for ONTAP file system recommended by a migration plan
description: Provision a migration plan by deploying the FSx for ONTAP file system or file systems it recommends for the target VMware cloud environment.

name: Edit the comment of a migration plan
description: Change the comment stored with a saved migration plan in the VMware planning center.

name: Estimate savings for an Amazon EVS environment
description: Use the savings calculator to estimate how much can be saved by running Amazon EVS with FSx for ONTAP storage.

name: Rename a VM inventory dataset
description: Give an uploaded VM inventory dataset in the VMware planning center a new name.

name: View the well-architected status of an EVS environment
description: Open the well-architected status tab for a discovered EVS environment to review its configuration against AWS and NetApp best practices and see remediation guidance.

name: Connect a sandbox clone to a CI/CD pipeline
description: Obtains the REST API code needed to connect a sandbox clone to CI/CD tools for automated software delivery.

name: Calculate storage cost savings with custom database host details
description: Uses the savings calculator with manually entered host details to compare the cost of the current database storage with FSx for ONTAP.

name: Explore storage cost savings for detected database hosts
description: Analyzes detected or uploaded SQL Server hosts on EBS, FSx for Windows or on-premises storage to estimate the savings of moving them to FSx for ONTAP.

name: Prepare SQL Server resources for protection with Backup and Recovery
description: Discovers resources, validates prerequisites and installs the SQL Server plug-in so SQL Server instances and databases can be protected with NetApp Backup and Recovery.

name: Check sandbox clone data integrity
description: Runs an integrity check on all objects in a sandbox clone to determine whether its data is intact and current.

name: Create a sandbox clone
description: Creates a sandbox clone of a source database on a target host for development and testing.

name: Create a user database
description: Creates a new user database with specified file settings in a managed Microsoft SQL Server instance.

name: Delete a sandbox clone
description: Deletes a sandbox clone.

name: Deregister a database resource
description: Removes a registered database resource from management.

name: Refresh a sandbox clone
description: Updates a sandbox clone with newer data from its source database.

name: Register a database resource
description: Authenticates and registers one or more SQL Server instances or Oracle databases so they can be monitored, protected and managed.

name: Revert a sandbox clone to its baseline
description: Re-baselines a sandbox clone, discarding changes and returning it to its original cloned state.

name: Split a sandbox clone
description: Splits a database clone from its source database so it becomes an independent database.

name: View sandbox clone connection information
description: Displays and copies the connection information of a sandbox clone.

name: Dismiss the analysis of a database configuration
description: Dismisses the well-architected analysis of specific database configurations that do not apply, so they no longer raise alerts or affect optimization results.

name: Fix a database configuration issue
description: Remediates database configurations that deviate from well-architected best practices on selected registered resources.

name: Perform a one-time configuration assessment of unregistered database hosts
description: Runs a downloadable assessment script on database hosts and uploads its results to get best-practice recommendations without registering resources or storing credentials.

name: Reactivate a dismissed database configuration analysis
description: Re-enables the well-architected analysis of a previously dismissed database configuration so it is evaluated again.

name: Run an on-demand configuration analysis of registered databases
description: Triggers an immediate well-architected analysis of registered database resources and shows the resulting recommendations.

name: Deploy a Microsoft SQL Server host
description: Deploys a new Microsoft SQL Server database host backed by FSx for ONTAP storage and enables remote connection to it.

name: Deploy a PostgreSQL server host
description: Deploys a new PostgreSQL server as a standalone instance or high-availability pair with FSx for ONTAP storage.

name: Analyze database error logs
description: Runs the error log analyzer on a SQL Server instance or Oracle database to review errors with AI-based explanations and suggested remediation.

name: Log in to File Analytics
description: The user logs in to the File Analytics GUI and sees the status of the NFS and SMB agents.

name: Add a file server to File Analytics
description: A file server is added to File Analytics so its shares can be scanned when planning a migration.

name: Configure XCP logging
description: An xcpLogConfig.json file is created to enable the chosen XCP logging features for NFS and SMB.

name: Run a File Analytics scan of a file share
description: A file share is scanned in File Analytics, which fills in the stat view and file distribution tabs for migration planning.

name: Configure the S3 connector
description: An S3 bucket and AWS CLI credentials are set up so that XCP can run with the S3 connector.

name: Configure SSO for File Analytics
description: File Analytics is registered with an enterprise identity provider so users can log in through single sign-on.

name: Configure the POSIX connector
description: The maximum number of open file descriptors is raised so that XCP can use the POSIX connector.

name: Configure the XCP NFS INI file
description: The XCP catalog location is set in the XCP NFS host INI configuration file and verified.

name: Install File Analytics for NFS
description: File Analytics for NFS is installed or upgraded on a Linux host and reachable from a browser.

name: Install File Analytics for SMB
description: The File Analytics SMB agent is freshly installed and licensed on a Windows host.

name: Install XCP NFS
description: XCP NFS is extracted, licensed and activated on a Linux host for a root or non-root user.

name: Install XCP SMB
description: XCP SMB and its Microsoft VC++ redistributable prerequisite are installed, licensed and activated on a Windows client.
